articleTitle: Partial Discharge Measurement and Signal Analysis at Repetitive Voltage Pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the measurement and evaluation of partial discharges with high frequency current transformers at square wave voltages. Since these voltages are used as power supply for electrical machines, especially in the field of drive systems, twisted pairs of enameled wires are used as test samples. In addition to the complex signal acquisition, it is important to evaluate the signals. For this purpose, the analysis in the time domain, in the frequency domain by means of fast Fourier transformation and in the time frequency domain by means of wavelet transformation are presented in this work. It is shown that the voltage shape of the test voltage has only a small effect on the spectrum of the pulse in the frequency range under consideration for the investigated twisted pairs.

articleTitle: Effects of Radial Divided Magnet Shifting on Cogging Torque of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Generator for Small Scale Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transitioning energy sources from fossil fuels to renewable energy is demanding currently due to global warming issues. Those require advanced technology of each component that supports renewable energy to achieve high efficiency, for example, permanent magnet generator (PM generator) for wind power plants. PM generator is widely known for high efficiency, high energy density, low maintenance, and simplicity. Although a PM generator has a lot of advantages, it still has drawbacks specifically for cogging torque generated between the permanent magnet and stator core which causes vibration and decreases the net torque from the shaft due to its counter direction from the rotor direction. Several methods have been proposed to reduce cogging torque such as traditional skewing magnet, selecting appropriate slot opening, pole arc to pole pitch ratio arrangement, and placing flux barrier between 2 slots. This paper discusses the implementation of radially divided magnet shifting to axial flux PM generator with yokeless and segmented armature configuration. The impact of magnet shifting on reducing the cogging torque is also discussed. The proposed design is a permanent magnet divided into 2, 3, 4, and 5 parts and shift the magnet with a common angle respected to the inner side of the magnet. 3D finite element analysis is performed to analyze and simulate the axial flux PM generator model. An Analytical approach is discussed further to satisfy the relationship between magnet common angle and generated cogging torque. The results show that higher number of divided permanent magnet leads to decreased cogging torque, although the smaller size of permanent magnet will be challenging in manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Corona Discharge Detection with Modified Consumer Cameras
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Corona discharges are a type of partial discharges (PD) on the surface of conductors. They are a common problem in high-voltage transmission systems and switch-gear due to the high electric field strength. Because of the emitted ozone and ultraviolet (UV) radiation, corona discharges lead to the degradation of polymeric insulators. They also generate undesired audible noise and radio frequency interference. Special cameras are available for the detection and localization of corona discharges on overhead lines and in air insulated substations. However, these cameras usually work with a beamsplitter, separate sensors for visible and UV light, highly UV transmissive quartz optics and solar-blind filters to be used in the day time. This makes them rather expensive. In this paper a modified consumer camera is presented as an alternative to specialized corona cameras. Regular digital camera sensors are naturally sensitive for UV (and infrared) radiation and can be used to detect discharges. Because of the adverse effects on the image quality, manufacturers usually implement filters on the sensor to block the UV light. These filters can be removed to greatly enhance the sensitivity of the camera. This paper aims to compare the two different technologies and their strengths and weaknesses and show some application examples.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Conventional Pumped-Storage Hydropower (C-PSH) and Ternary Pumped-Storage Hydropower (T-PSH) Systems Integrated with Wind Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The impact of renewable energy resources and energy storage systems (ESS) on power system operation is examined in this study, with a focus on their ability to provide primary frequency reserve, alleviate capacity needs, manage congestion, support voltage and reactive power, and enhance reliability at reduced costs. Specifically, the integration of wind energy with ternary pumped-storage hydropower (T-PSH) and conventional pumped-storage hydropower (C-PSH) systems is assessed using a 10-bus system and GE Positive Sequence Load Flow (PSLF) software. Various contingency scenarios, including wind farm generation loss and loss of load, are considered to evaluate the performance of the system. The study aims to optimize the dynamic models and grid connection of PSH systems to maximize their effectiveness and fulfill grid load requirements.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Solar Power Generation System on Tello Island
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesia’s electricity service provider, PLN (Perusahaan Listrik Negara), plans to conduct more environmentally friendly business activities. PLN intends to use hybrid schemes with batteries and convert diesel power plants to renewable energy sources in isolated power systems. This aims to reduce fossil fuel usage and improve power generation cost efficiency. Tello Island is one of 200 locations chosen for the project as a research area due to its isolated power system and the fuel consumption of the existing diesel generator in the first phase. This paper discusses the process of designing a hybrid solar power system on Tello Island. The main objective of this design process is determining and optimizing the hybrid solar power generation system’s capacity according to existing system conditions and component capacity available in the market. The designed system consists of an existing 1,524kW diesel generator system, 2,207.25kWp photovoltaic modules, 1,800kW grid inverter, 2,064kWh battery, and 800kW battery inverter. With those designed configurations of the hybrid system, the operating time of the existing diesel power plant had reduced from 24 hours to just 15 hours. Not only that, but the designed system also has better economic parameter values compared to the existing system. Future development of this project’s results can be carried out by adjusting the designed hybrid solar power generation system to load developments that occur in real-life on Tello Island’s power system.

articleTitle: Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis on the Improvement of Hybrid Savonius-Darrieus NREL S809 at Various Fluid Flows
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Among all types of vertical axis wind turbines, Savonius and Darrieus are the most popular to study. Savonius has a very large torque and requires a low wind velocity to start the rotation, but the efficiency is below 20%. Meanwhile, Darrieus is not capable of self-starting if the wind velocity is below 4 m/s, but the efficiency is the best among all types of vertical axis wind turbines, which is around 40–45%. So far, many researchers have applied the hybrid Savonius-Darrieus to combine their performances. However, the conventional hybrid Savonius-Darrieus cannot produce an optimal Power Coefficient at a high Tip Speed Ratio. In this study, an improvement in the performance of the hybrid Savonius-Darrieus has been analyzed using the Computational Fluid Dynamics method at various fluid flows. This improvement was carried out with the aim of obtaining a high Moment Coefficient and Power Coefficient in all turbine Tip Speed Ratios compared to the conventional hybrid Savonius-Darrieus. The hybrid model used is the 2-bladed Savonius as the internal rotor and the 3-bladed Darrieus NREL S809 as the external rotor with a rotor radius ratio of 0.5. Improvements were made by changing the turbine rotation mode from hybrid at a low Tip Speed Ratio to single Darrieus at a high Tip Speed Ratio. This method was tested in the wind velocity range of 3–7 m/s using the Realizable k-e turbulence model, enhanced wall treatment. As a result, the best performance occurs at a wind velocity of 7 m/s, which is a Moment Coefficient value of 110% better than single Darrieus at low TSR and a maximum Power Coefficient value of 50% better than conventional hybrid.

articleTitle: Optimizing Local Renewable Energy Resources for Reducing Energy Dependency on An Isolated Island: A Case Study of Saumlaki Island, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Saumlaki system is located on a small remote island that experiences an electricity supply crisis. Another problem faced in the Saumlaki system is energy dependency on fossil fuels supplied from other islands. To overcome these problems, it is necessary to use local renewable energy resources. However, using renewable energy resources potentially increase the generation cost. Therefore, a well-planned generation expansion planning that optimizes local RES in Saumlaki is necessary to achieve an optimal generation mix and cost. Therefore, this research addresses this issue and aims to find an optimal power development plan in the Saumlaki system by maximizing local RE resources and reducing its energy dependency on external sources. The optimization in this research is done through the MILP method with a planning horizon starting in 2023 to 2032. The research results show a decrease in generation costs from 16.36 cents/kWh to 8.81 cents/kWh. Biomass power plants play a crucial role in supplying electricity in Saumlaki with reliable, sustainable, and eco-friendly energy. Using local biomass energy has also helped reduce the Saumlaki system's reliance on HSD energy imported from other islands. This is demonstrated by the decrease in the proportion of HSD in the energy mix from 100% to only 45% in 2032, achieved through the use of 55% biomass energy, which amounts to 30.7 GWh.

articleTitle: Determining Optimal Generation Cost in Power Systems With Shares of Variable Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Thermal Power plants provide safe and continuous operation regardless of the load profile. They guarantee stability to the electrical system. However, the projections of the government in overcoming the environmental crisis in the future with the massive addition of Variable Renewable Energy Powerplant such as solar, wind, and some hydropower will change the load profile of the thermal power plants on the system. Electricity market stakeholders are dealing with new challenges related to increasing variability in both production and load demand. Increasing generation rates of variable renewable energy sources (VRES) cause net load fluctuations that need to be supplied in real time by other resources. Currently, reserve requirements have been determined using deterministic criteria such as percentage of peak load or largest unit loss. This paper discusses the method to determine operating reserves to overcome the variability of EBT generators without neglecting the optimization of generation costs. The study is conducted on Java - Bali power systems with a maximum 5% share of Renewable Energy, the results shows that determined optimal generation cost is lower than Busines as usual (BaU) scenario. The estimated optimal generation cost is USD119Million /year in 2025 and USD 62 Million/year in 2030, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparison of Solar Power Meter and Intelligence Solar Power Meter and Its Impact on Solar Photovoltaic Design
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The terrestrial measurement of solar irradiation power in the selected location is crucial for the solar photovoltaic power plant design. However, it should be carried out manually onsite using the current Solar Power Meter (SPM). A device that can record this value remotely online is needed to ensure more efficient work. Hence, an Intelligent Solar Power Meter (ISPM) using a BH1750 sensor equipped with a cover in the form of an LED light cover was designed. The terrestrial measurement using both devices along with satellite measurement has been carried out in the Merangin site for performance comparison purposes. The result showed that the difference between each device in measuring the probability distribution, the financial model and the intermittent profile is less than 5%, with data that can be monitored remotely using internet connected IoT features.

articleTitle: Optimization Of Photovoltaic Types Of Solar Modules For Batteries On Load Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Solar power plants with an Off-Grid system utilize batteries as a storage medium for energy produced from photovoltaic modules because the system is offgrid. In this study, tests were carried out using VRLA (Valve Regulated Lead Acid) and lithium batteries with linear and non-linear loads by using Polycrystalline and Monocrystalline modules. From the observation of 4 experimental data that we can analyze for a more optimal PLTS system circuit using Monocrystalin solar panels and using Lithium batteries because of the measurement data shows that optimal current and voltage for PV absorption and output is greater than that others with the same average irradiation and the same load used. For loads that are used from several types of linear and non-linear loads with the same capacity of10 watts which are absorbed more from the battery output are non-linear loads (Balast lamps and Incandescent lamps (AC) compared to LED lamps. For a longer and optimal battery use Lithium batteries because the current coming out of the lithium is always stable and there is a battery management system in the cells of the lithium battery and input and output from the inverter is more optimal by using lithium batteries.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of High Voltage Motors Utilizing Corona Camera to Determine the Precise Location of Insulation Surface Discharge as the Basis for Undertaking the Appropriate Repair
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Partial discharge activity is an indication of an ‘incipient fault’ in high voltage insulation and is widely regarded as the best ‘early warning’ indicator of the deterioration of high voltage insulation [1]. Several technologies for detecting partial discharge had been developed and implemented however, to conduct precise maintenance on high voltage motor insulation, precise information is required, such as the type of partial discharge event that has occurred and the precise location where it has occurred. Online partial discharge, offline partial discharge monitoring, and corona camera inspection are employed. These three techniques combine and supplement one another to provide data on the characteristics and location of the partial discharge. Through obtaining this kind of information, we would be able to perform the appropriate repairs on the motor to reduce the likelihood of motor failure during motor in services. Based on a number of observations and comparisons using the instruments and equipment mentioned in this paper, we have determined that the comparative severity of partial discharge counts ranges from 0 to 32,000. Using this measurement method, the benchmark condition monitoring based on the corona camera can be evaluated further for repair planning and other strategic actions. Condition monitoring is a maintenance method by relying on trending data or data clusters from the same type of equipment, the same data collection method.

articleTitle: Design of 1 kWp Solar Water Pump System for Land Irrigation in Banjaran
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: A terraced rice field in Banjaran, Bandung Regency, Indonesia, suffers from drought during the dry season. The only water source during the dry season is a river that is located at the lowest point of the terraced rice field. A water pump is needed to transfer the water from the river to the water tank which is located at the highest point. A 1 kWp off-grid solar photovoltaic (PV) system with 3,600 Wh battery system and 5 kL water tank is designed to supply the water pump. The performance of the system was evaluated through PVSyst simulation and tested in the field. Results show that the system is capable of providing 6,580 L water when it was operated from 10 a.m.to 2 p.m. daily. During the dry season, the solar water pump has successfully supplied the water for land irrigation. The water produced is sufficient for crop irrigation, specifically corn, and the system can be scaled up for the rice field irrigation. The reliability of the system makes it promising alternative to conventional irrigation system for small-scale farming in the region.

articleTitle: The Stability Analysis of The Maximum Integration of Intermittent and Non-Dispatchable Power Plant in the Iconic Isolated Island Grid, Nusa Penida
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Since Nusa Penida Island have a complete resources of intermittent and non-dispatchable energy resources such as wind and solar energy then maximum integration of such power plant is possible to develop. However, the stability of the grid will be considerations of grid operator. On the research, based on stability of microgrid standard, which is endorsed by IEEE Smart Grid, the stability of the grid during possible disturbance had modelling and simulated. The results show without any stability controller and defense scheme, the grid will be face instability condition during part of disturbance. Hence, the maximum integration of intermittent and non-dispatchable power plant in the isolated island only possible and allowable if the advanced grid controller or defense scheme is applied in the grid.

articleTitle: Determining Localization and Measuring Level of Partial Discharge in Power Transformer Using Acoustic Sensor: Case Studies at Kemang & Cilegon Baru Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The dielectric subsystem is an essential part of every HV apparatus. Along with the operation time, some deterioration can happen to the dielectric section. Offline tests can measure how good the dielectric is, but some symptoms cannot be discovered. Partial discharge (PD) is a standard test that can measure the dielectric strength of all equipment. When PD energy is high enough, failure can happen. PD test can determine the location of the source and the best follow-up for repairing this issue—the concept for localizing the PD source inside a transformer using the screening area method. Testing equipment consists of four acoustic sensors installed on every side of the transformer. Acoustic signals from the creep source will travel in dielectric oil and creep to the metal surface of the transformer tank, where they can be detected and measured with acoustic sensors. When one or more sensors detect a more significant PD signal, all sensors move to that side and measure a wide area. This step will repeat, moving the sensor from a comprehensive place to a smaller area depending on where it detects a partial discharge signal until it reaches a specific area where all sensors detect a PD source. This paper gives steps for localizing the PD source and findings. At the Kemang substation, dissolved gas analysis (DGA) and sweep frequency response analysis (SFRA) correlate with PD measurements. Research from the Duval triangle and PD measurement has the same result: low discharge level at phase T (high voltage side), supported by the SFRA test with a small deterioration result. In another case at Cilegon Baru Substation, a major-level PD source was found at the tertiary voltage side of all three banks of transformers and matched with a high level of paper degradation findings.

articleTitle: Assessing Transformer Insulation Aging through Oil Treatment Index: A Comparative and Correlation Study of 150 kV Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Power transformers are important electrical equipment with a high investment value in the electrical system. Manufacturers design transformers to operate for many years, but the aging factors of the transformer can trigger operational failures. Such failures result in significant losses and disrupt the distribution of electrical energy to consumers. To prevent this, it is necessary to assess the aging of the transformer through its insulation material, namely oil. Three factors—chemical, electrical, and physical—affect the condition of transformer oil insulation. The frequently tested oil insulation parameters were observed, such as interfacial tension (IFT), color, breakdown voltage (BDV), acidity, and moisture content. The scoring matrix method in CIGRE TB 761 was implemented to obtain power transformer oil treatment index (OTI) from those five oil tests. This study then analyzes the correlation between OTI (Oil Treatment Index) as well as each oil parameter to the transformer operating age. This study also compares and evaluates three sets of previously proposed weighting factors. The implementation and analysis is done to 55 data points of 150 kV power transformers.

articleTitle: An Approach to Define the Criticality Parameter from Business Values in an Asset-Intensive Utility
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: An asset-intensive utility must manage risks with limited resources to achieve its objectives. The risk related to an in-service asset’s failure, or asset risk, is the primary consideration to be addressed. Asset criticality provides information about the consequences of an individual asset failure to the business. The business values define the parameters of asset criticality, for example, reliability, safety, environment, and finances. This paper provides a quantification of asset criticality in a vertically integrated electricity utility with a case study owned by PLN Indonesia. The quantification focuses on two criticality parameters: the consequence of an asset’s failure in terms of Energy Not Served (ENS) and Extra Fuel Cost (EFC). The case study comprises four interconnected power systems with thousands of individual generation units, power transformers, and transmission line segments. A software simulation calculated the ENS and the EFC by simulating an N1 failure on each individual asset. The result from the simulation was MW instant that later being converted into a Monetary unit per hour. The information about asset criticality helps the organization prioritize investment, operation and maintenance, and power system operation decisions.

articleTitle: Development Of Generation Technology On Smart Network Using Smart Micro Grid In Renewable Energy Laboratory Institut Teknologi PLN
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Summary of research Integration of renewable microgrid systems in the main electricity system is a study of the integration of microgrid systems in the main electricity system using renewable resources. This research aims to improve the reliability of electricity supply, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and reduce dependence on fossil energy sources. Research shows that the integration of renewable microgrid systems into the main electricity system provides various benefits, including increasing energy efficiency, reliability of electricity supply, and reducing carbon emissions. However, microgrid integration on a large scale also comes with challenges such as costs and enabling policies. This study concludes that the integration of a renewable microgrid system into the main electricity system is an effective way to utilize renewable energy and increase the reliability of electricity supply. However, there is a need for appropriate policy and regulatory support to support widespread use of this system. For this reason, it is necessary to conduct trials for the pilot project. In the development of Smart Microgrid System Technology with several of our hybrid generators at the PLN Jakarta Institute of Technology Laboratory, it is necessary to carry out trials and work together with PLN R&D and other agencies such as the New and Renewable Energy Conversion Center of the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources to find out that they can synchronize electricity from Photovoltaics with electricity from PLN for the development of smart grid equivalent generation system technology with Smart Microgrid.

articleTitle: Distribution Transformer Assessment and Risk Identification in PT PLN (Persero) UID Banten
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The distributions transformer is one of the mains equipment for the 20 kV distribution system. Transformer conditions are expected in good condition to prevent unexpected transformer damage. The cause of transformer damage may vary but in PT PLN (Persero) UID Banten transformers damage is mainly due to low insulation resistance and heat due to load unbalance. Low insulation resistance can be caused by the quality of the transformer oil, winding wire insulation quality, and water and salt content. Insulation resistance decreased and overheated can be prevented by conducting a thorough diagnostic by testing the oil and winding insulation resistance. The result from the diagnostic can give information about the transformer reliability index scale. Condition assessment of the distribution transformer includes diagnosis and risk identification. Diagnosis compares transformer condition to transformer standard. The results from the diagnosis are used in risk identification. All information from the assessment creates a clear priority scale for the maintenance timeline of the Distribution Transformer.

articleTitle: Investigation Properties of Silicone Elastomer Insulation with Difference Composition Nanofiller SiO2+ATH Under Artificial Tropical Climate Aging
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Outdoor polymer insulators are often subject to various stresses such as severe environments and corona discharges that can alter the chemical structure of basic polymer and degrade surface properties. Considering the most significant influences from the tropical environment, significant changes in the dielectric and mechanical properties can be observed indicating bulk defects of the materials. This paper investigates the level of composition of $\mathrm {SiO_{2}}$ nanofillers and alumina trihydrate (ATH) nanofiller on silicone elastomers to improve their properties as outdoor high-voltage insulators. We have created test material from the resin of silicone rubber RTV683 with a mixture of nano silica powder (20 nm) and nano ATH powder (20-30 nm). The stoichiometric ratio of resin, filler, and hardener compositions varied (80-95: 5-20: 3-7.5). To determine its performance, the specimens were aged in the test chamber with given ambient conditions (relative humidity from 70±5 to 90±5%, temperature from 50 to 70°C, high-voltage stress of 20 kV and UV radiation) simultaneously during 720 hours (30 days). The experiment results showed that the absorption of moisture in the silicone elastomer of different filler content varied from 0.06% to 0.36%, Samples with higher filler content showed higher moisture absorption. The dielectric properties (relative permittivity is 3-4) and the hydrophobicity of the silicon elastomeric surface did not decrease under the pressure of the artificial tropical climate, even the contact angle of the water droplets increased (>90° the mechanical properties (tensile strength) were 1.22-2.54 N/mm$^{2}$). The phenomenon of scattering of nanofiller particles on the sample surface was analyzed by SEM, EDX and FTIR.

articleTitle: Designing Harmonic Filters on LED Lamp Loads to Reduce Odd Order THD
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In a decade, the global lighting industry has undergone a total revolution with the arrival of LED lighting. Indonesia is also undergoing this profound transformation but these light sources are non-linear loads which generate high harmonic currents. These non-linear loads which generate non simusoidal voltage waveforms, which can be harmful to other loads connected to the power grid. The objective of this research is to design a harmonic filter to mitigate the harmonic impact of using LED lamps based on the Indonesian standard SNI IEC 61000-3-2:2014. We have tested five types of the most common household LED lamps in the Indonesian market. The methods in this research use Power Qualty Analyzer to measure the power quality were measured, such as total power consumption and total harmonic distortion for current (THDi) and total harmonic distortion for voltage (THDv), factor of power, the harmonics. The search uses a passive filter to reduce harmonic values by determining the appropriate filter parameter (R, L, and C). The expected result of this research is the reduction of the harmonic content using a filter designed to meet the requirements of the standards.

articleTitle: Practical Approach in Setting Asset Management System and Capability in a State-Owned Utility
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Despite being implemented in various organizations worldwide for over two decades, asset management is considered a new approach in Indonesia. Not many organizations implement and take advantage of implementing this approach. Among others are oil and gas company, power generation, transportation, and operational units of electricity utility. These organizations start by managing assets because it fits their roles and aims for reliability. However, such an aim is only sometimes true for a company that provides a specific service and assets that are part of a plant to deliver this service. Certainly not for PLN, as a state-owned electricity utility. PLN stakeholders comprise the Government, customers, suppliers, mass media, society, and financial institutions. The shareholder is the Ministry of Finance, while the regulators are the Ministry of Energy & Mineral Resources and the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprise. Hence, PLN’s challenge is to be able to identify and manage varying stakeholders’ requirements, which sometimes against one another. A very tight set of targets, including the completion time, have pushed PLN to find the most effective measures to complete the tasks. As an asset-intensive utility, one of the measures is implementing asset management. PLN, as a corporate, started its asset management journey in 2021. Based on the gap assessment against ISO 55001 and 39 subjects AM Landscape results, an implementation program is developed. However, setting up the asset management system and capabilities as part of the program has never been easy, not only because of a wide range of requirements but also due to the local culture. This paper will discuss how the specific approach needs to be applied to succeed in the setup.

articleTitle: Analysis of Virtual Inertia Control System to Maintain Frequency Stability System Connected with pump
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Electric submersible pump (ESP) widely used for oil and gas industry utilities. Operational of ESP must be maintained to ensure production activity not disturbed. When ESP were operating, the frequency of induction motor may change caused by dynamic loads. The rate change of frequency (RoCoF) from ESP caused frequency system oscillating. To overcome frequency oscillation problem, this paper will propose secondary control. Virtual inertia control (VIC) choosen to overcome frequency oscillation problem caused by ESP operations. VIC have fast respond dynamic frequency. Frequency stability analysis will considered to analyze performance of VIC. Applying VIC into system will reduce frequency oscillation at power line.

articleTitle: A Proper Lightning Arrester Placement to Protect Traction Substation in Jakarta Bandung High Speed Railway System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: To prevent damage that could cause system outage, the traction substation must be protected from lightning. This study calculates the lightning voltage that the transformer at the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway (JBHSR) traction substation will receive with the current arrester arrangement. To safeguard the transformer and other equipment, it is advised that lightning arresters be strategically placed. The study’s findings offer suggestions for safeguarding traction substation equipment against lightning disturbances. Also highlighted are the JBHSR traction substation’s current problems. To increase the reliability and efficiency of the railway, the study’s findings can be utilized as a guide when designing the protective distance of the lightning arrester at traction substation to prevent incoming lightning waves.

articleTitle: Effect of Localised Soil on the Measured and Calculated Resistance Values
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In designing the ground electrodes, soil resistivity is the first parameter to be assessed in the design of grounding systems. The soil resistivity profile determines the conductivity of the soil in a large area, however localised soil around the ground electrode can be expectedly different from the representation of the conductivity of the soil mass. Hence, differences between the measured and calculated ground resistance at low magnitude of voltage and current, and at low frequency, RDC values are likely to be expected. In IEEE Standard 81, several possible reasons were listed that are thought to be the causes of differences between the measured and calculated ground resistance values, however limited study was found in identifying the main cause of these differences. Localised soil around the ground electrode has also not been clearly considered in the literature as one of the main reasons that contribute to differences in measured and calculated RDC values. For this reason, this paper attempts to address this shortfall. Firstly, a compilation of the previously published work on the measured and computed RDC values is presented, where the percentage differences between the measured and calculated RDC can be seen for various RDC values. Secondly, the effect of localised soil surrounding the ground electrode, which was done by adding other types of soil around the ground electrodes will be investigated. Percentage differences between calculated and measured RDC values can be observed for the electrode installed in natural and when other types of soil were added surround the ground electrode.

articleTitle: Energy Demand and Emission Analysis of Train Electrification in Java Island
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transport sector still relies heavily on fossil fuels and is responsible for Indonesia’s greenhouse gasses (GHG) emission, hence the train electrification in Java Island is necessary to decarbonize the transport sector. In addition, the train electrification potentially overcomes the oversupply in the Java-Madura-Bali (JAMALI) power system. In this paper, the power demand analysis of the train electrification is presented. The calculations are based on the trains schedule and the locomotive types. The proposed train electrification increases energy demand up to 2.91 GWh/day. The power demand daily profile shows the peak demand is 207.45 MW at 21.30 and the lowest demand is 134.73 MW at 03.50. The electrification is able to absorb the excess energy from the JAMALI power system and reduce the dependence on diesel fuel supply. The total diesel fuel saving made with the train electrification is 422.69 kL/day or 154,281.9 kL/year. The emission analysis show that the emission from the consumption of the diesel fuel is equivalent to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions of 1,180.80s tons/day while from the electrification of trains is 2,074.33 tons per day. To reduce the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission, it is not only the train electrification that is matter, but also increasing the penetration of renewable energy in the JAMALI power system.

articleTitle: Engineering Study of Rooftop Photovoltaic “Study Case in Elementary School, Jakarta”
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Government has decided to develop renewable energy for ensure the mix energy target 23% in 2025 can be realized. The government regulations based on Perpres No. 22 Year 2007 or Presidential Regulation No. 22 Year 2007, Rencana Umum Energi Nasional (RUEN) or National General Energy Plan, mentioned that 30% of rooftop capacity government building must be installed for rooftop photovoltaic. Furthermore the electricity energy price will increase year by year because the more expensive of fuel price the more expensive of energy price. In Indonesia most of the power plant still use fossil fuel such as coal, gas and MFO (Marine Fuel Oil), which is the fuel price is getting more expensive year by year also the CO2 emission issue become serious problem in future. Hence, rooftop photovoltaic modeling has needed for not only government building but also residential building in order to give solution for electricity energy problem and reduce fossil fuel for electricity supply. The objective of this paper is to analyze the engineering design and study the economic rooftop photovoltaic in school building. This research will give some contribution for electricity customer in industry scale and residential scale, how the photovoltaic can be installed and what the advantage for use this system. Some method will be used for initiating this research i.e literature study from previous research, collect data research and use the software to analyze the data. Software homer will be used to give some consideration about decision making for the technical and economical study. Monthly cost of electricity saving for this school about Rp 1.960.000 or 51,6 % from previous tariff without using rooftop photovoltaic system.

articleTitle: Implementation of Certainty Level on Transformer Health Index on the Basis of Oil Quality Factor in Kalsulmapana Region
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformer Health Index which is developed for Kalsulmapana Transmission Division focusing on oil quality factors (OQF) including 5 parameters, namely: ACID, IFT, WATER, BDV, COLOR. Since the completeness of all parameters cannot be fulfilled, certainty level (CL) needs to be applied to gain equal assessment results between transformers. Both OQF and CL parameters have been developed in previous paper and have been validated. This paper utilizes a developed method for evaluating the transformer’s health condition based on the results of transformer oil tests that have been carried out. The case study refers to 20 transformer units in the Kalsulmapana region according to the 2022 test data to get an overview of the health index and reliability of the transformer. Based on oil quality measurement of 20 transformers, it is found that more than 90% of the transformers are in good condition and only 10% of the transformers are in bad condition. As the certainty level for 20 transformers, it has a balanced composition between high and low values. The combination of OQF and CF forms a classification of conditions that recommends different treatment actions.

articleTitle: Low-cost Harmonic Generator for Education Using MyRIO
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The existence of harmonic disturbances in the power system has many losses that cannot be ignored, giving rise to many studies on reducing harmonics. The first step in examining harmonic disturbances is to understand how the harmonic wave is formed, and one way is by modeling mathematical equations in simulation applications such as Simulink, Matlab, or others. However, the modeling method using Fast Fourier Transform in the simulation application has shortcomings because the analysis process is only based on the results of the harmonic signal waveform plot. In this research, the mathematical model for forming harmonic waves is implemented on a controller, namely myRio, using Labview, which has an analog output so that the formation of harmonic waves is not only displayed but generated through an analog output continuously for a more comprehensive analysis process, one of which is to test the active power filter by providing a reference signal. The simulation of harmonic signal formation using myRio will be helpful for research needs in reducing harmonic disturbances in the electricity network or for educational needs. Based on the test results, the error value between the set point amplitude of each odd order of harmonics determined by the harmonic signal that has been issued through the analog output of myRio is an average of below 10% for odd order. The test results are taken from tests carried out by forming a harmonic signal wave with the same amplitude value at every odd harmonic order except the fundamental.

articleTitle: Study of Generator Lifetime In Combined Cycle Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: A generator is an equipment used to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy which in operation experiences electrical, mechanical and thermal stress which results in a decrease in the quality of the insulation of the generator stator winding. Stator insulation failure is one of the main causes of generator failure. Tests of insulation resistance and polarity index, tan delta, partial discharge, wedge tightness and polarization depolarization current are used to analyze the condition of generator stator isolation and can predict life time by analyzing the test results. So failure can be detected early and planned treatment accordingly. The test results show that the condition of the generator stator isolation in phase T in humid conditions is indicated by the polarity index test results of 1.45. For phase R, it is indicated that carefull category partial discharge occurred at the end-winding caused by conductive contamination with a discharge charge of 161.8 nC. The results of the wedges tightness test 5 experienced loosness and 2 experienced looseness. Meanwhile, the remaining life of the generator winding insulation is predicted to be 3 years with a record of normal operation and no disturbance to the generator.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Evaluation of In-City EV Charging Station Empowered by PV-based Microgrid in Various Solar Irradiation Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The transition energy to ultra-low and zero vehicle emissions brings over a challenging situation to develop public electric vehicle charging stations (SPKLU) infrastructure. A plug-in electric charging infrastructure solar panel supported microgrid might offer a potential solution. An integrated microgrid with PV sources, battery charging, and EVs has been designed using a simulation that can be mobilized through order to meet the needs and expansion load. This research will be focused on the technical evaluation and financing scheme comparation to define the best solution for in-city EV charging station. Using techno-economic approach, the project implementation criteria at PLN can be met by the financial indicators resulting in IDR 17 billion NPV higher than 0, with 11.2 years payback period less than 15 years, and 13.64% IRR on equity higher than current cost capital (7.1%). Finally, the result indicate that the solar irradiation value and price of photovoltaics have a significant impact with effectiveness and design of EV charging station empowered by PV-based microgrid in three different Indonesia urban areas (Jakarta, Bandung, and Denpasar) with level of radiation in each areas.

articleTitle: Security of The Bali Electrical System From Interference Of 4 Marine Electricity Cables with the Adaptive Defense Scheme of The Bali Island
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)

authors.preferredName: I Gde Made Yoga Semadhi Artha

abstract: The Adaptive Defense Scheme (ADS) is a dynamic and adaptive system defense scheme in which island conditions release the load in real time to maintain a balance between electricity generation and load usage, or release the load in real time until the maximum operating power has been determined. ADS Island Bali is an effort to save the load if there is a disturbance in the N-4 submarine cable Conditions, where the submarine cable is one of the energy supply channels from the island of Java to Bali. ADS equipment already uses IED (Intelligent Electronic Device) which has IEC 61850 Protocol, and IED ADS communication system uses GOOSE. The benefit of implementing ADS Island Bali is to prevent PLN from losing a maximum of 915.8 MW of Energy Not Served and to maintain the stability of Bali’s electricity so that it can support community economic activities.

articleTitle: Discovery of LED Lighting: a History of Science between Research, Work and Serendipity
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The history of science is often made up of chance and that of the discovery of LED lighting is no exception to this rule. The declaration of birth of LED lighting appeared where it was not expected: in the cradle of telecommunications. From the end of the 19th century until the beginning of the 1960s, the only interest motivating research around diodes was the detection and amplification of electromagnetic signals for transmission and wireless telecommunications. This article traces the history of LED lighting in three main stages from the discoverers to the world revolution of LED lighting, passing through the passage to the commercial stage of LEDs as indicator lights. Through the history of LED lighting, this article also carries a useful reflection in the fields of research in general, theoretical or experimental, where work constitutes the fundamental pillar but where to keep a vigilant, aware, attentive and curious gaze on fortuitous discoveries made on the margins of research subjects is also very important.

articleTitle: A Method to Quantify Data Quality in Asset Health Indices Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Asset Health-Indexing is a data-intensive process. Depending on the complexity of the asset and the number of failure modes included in the model, the number of condition indicators involved in the process can be in the range of tens to hundreds. Consequently, data quality becomes a critical factor in the model’s output accuracy. The issues include incomplete data, old data, incorrect data format, and data validity. Therefore, measuring the data quality level can benefit the decision-maker. This paper introduces a method to quantify data quality in the asset health indices (AHI) model. The technique considers six data quality parameters: completeness, consistency, uniqueness, validity, accuracy, and timeliness. The output is the data quality indices, shown in % for each data quality parameter. The paper provides the implementation of the method in a power transformer AHI model from a case study in PLN Indonesia. The paper suggests that the data quality indices become an additional flag in the AHI modeling to assist the decision-maker in justifying better.

articleTitle: Optimization of Generating Unit System Locations to Convert Conventional Loop Distribution Networks to Radial Using Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The purpose of a load current analysis study is to obtain information about the power flow or voltage of a power grid. This information is necessary to evaluate the performance of your electrical system. Power flow problems involve calculating system currents and system voltages at a particular end station or distribution network bus where power losses are common. These power losses affect the quality of power service to consumers and the voltage difference when connecting the two buses.. in a radially distributed system. A closed power distribution system is one of the promising technologies to overcome the weaknesses of radial power distribution system. The transformation of conventional ring-distributed systems to radial systems is an interesting area of research for solving the problems that arise in a targeted manner. In this article, we use PSO (Particle Swarm optimization) algorithm to reconfigure the power distribution network to optimize the primary radial power distribution system with different voltages between the two buses and connect it to the loop power distribution network system and vice versa. I suggest that you allow it to connect to The proposed PSO-based algorithm was tested in an IEEE-33 radial-bus distribution system, and the power loss before reconfiguration was 208.4592kW, but after reconfiguration, with a minimum voltage of 0.91075 pooches before reconfiguration, he was 138.9275kW. So the reconfigured result is 0.94234 pu, but the simulated result is 36.2 seconds.

Author Keywords: Load Flow Analysis and Distributed Generated

articleTitle: Mitigation of the Potential for Sudden High-Temperature Hotspots on Substation Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Thermovision is carried out routinely to monitor hot spot anomalous conditions or hotspots on equipment. Several hotspot anomaly findings with category III suddenly occur in the conductor clamps. From the evaluation and mitigation carried out, several settings and measurement methods were found that were not uniform and did not match the proper setup. Errors in the settings and measurements of this measuring instrument cause the measurement data to be invalid so that it has the potential to be unable to accurately detect hotspot conditions. This paper describes several mitigation steps taken to follow up on the sudden occurrence of category III hotspots. Prediction of temperature rise using linear regression is also proposed to be able to help estimate the temperature increase based on the increase in current in the substation components.

articleTitle: Risk-Based Prioritization Method for Rescheduling Delayed Preventive Maintenance of Electric Power Transmission Assets
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: PT PLN (Persero) West Java Transmission Main Unit (UITJBB) is one of the units of PT PLN (Persero) that has a strategic role in the electricity business in DKI Jakarta and Banten. UITJBB serves VVIP, Zero Down Time Area, High Voltage Consumers, and Regular Consumers. Being part of a strategic electricity system, UITJBB’s core business is to distribute electricity from power plants to consumers in the western part of Java and ensure the availability and reliability of transmission equipment. To maintain the reliability and availability of the equipment, there are two types of maintenance applied in UITJBB, namely time-based maintenance and condition-based maintenance. Time-based maintenance is conducted at certain intervals, such as conducting maintenance on transformers every 2 years. All procedures and standards for performing preventive maintenance have been explained in the PLN Director’s Decision. However, due to the complexity of the transmission network and the criticality of the customers served, not all of the item able to be tested. Furthermore, due to the workability i.e., planned outage for maintenance, the time-based maintenance could not be executed. This problem will impact the difficulties to assess the asset condition (health index). There is risk that we cannot measure the ageing of the asset. Delayed preventive maintenance has become a recurring problem every year. The risk of damage to substation and transmission equipment due to the lack of preventive maintenance. In 2019, it was recorded that 33 percent of preventive maintenance was delayed out of the total planned maintenance, with 47 percent of the cases caused by system conditions and 22 percent caused by standby time. Rescheduling of delayed preventive maintenance is not optimal because there is no comprehensive and quantitative method available. This paper discusses the approach used to assess the risk of assets due to deferred maintenance, the increased risk value if maintenance is delayed for too long, and considerations for rescheduling. The expected result from this method is to reschedule the postponed preventive maintenance based on risk assessment, so that it becomes more optimal and serves as a basis for decision-making for the management to align with the company’s values.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Formation of Aging Products in Mineral Oil and Decane Stressed by Thermal Transformer Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The generation of fault gases in the well-known conventional mineral oils due to different transformer fault types is well established and there are a number of dissolved-gas-analysis(DGA) interpretation algorithms for an early fault detection of the power transformer. However, new alternative insulation liquids show different gassing behaviors due to various transformer faults. Especially, a thermal hot spot fault is one of the most important transformer faults and the classification into the different temperature ranges is essential for a reliable fault detection and condition evaluation of the transformer. This study shows that not only the various types of insulation differ in their gas formation behavior as a result of thermal faults, but also within mineral oils large differences are observed in the generation of defect gases, their concentration and ratios. In addition to the conventional fault gases, also higher-value C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> to C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> hydrocarbons are formed that also offer characteristic fault gases. Four different mineral oils, including naphthenic and paraffinic based mineral oils, were investigated regarding their gassing behavior due to various Hot-Spot-temperature. Large differences were apparent when comparing the two mineral oils types. Paraffinic based mineral oils generate a higher amount and also further fault gases in comparison to the naphthenic based mineral oils. Thus, in addition pure n-decane were also stressed by the same thermal faults and the formed fault gases were compared with the various mineral oils. High amounts of the characteristic fault gases as in the paraffin-based mineral oils are also detected in pure n-decane, so that alcanes appear to be mainly involved as a reactant in the aging mechanisms. This result leads to the conclusion that oil-specific DGA interpretation schemes are required that also consider the main constituents of the mineral oil.

articleTitle: Computation of Dielectric Constant of Cross-linked Epoxy resin through Molecular Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Cross-linked epoxy resins are widely used in various industrial applications. In high voltage power apparatus, reliability of the system is predicted from the health of its electrical insulation material, which can be estimated through electrical properties like dielectric constant. An understanding on the manner in which the dielectric constant of a material changes with various parameters like ageing, or incorporation of fillers, would help in life prediction or estimation of composite properties. To this end, the current work is a first step towards estimation of the dielectric constant of neat unaged epoxy through molecular-level simulations. Molecular Dynamic (MD) simulations provide insight into the study of materialistic properties at the nanoscale. An unaged sample of neat epoxy is prepared in this study through MD simulations. Physical epoxy resin samples are also prepared in the authors’ laboratory. The computed density of this MD sample, for both cured and uncured conditions, is validated with the experimental measurements. Further, the cross-linked equilibrated MD sample of neat unaged epoxy is used to compute the dielectric constant. The computed dielectric constant is validated with experimental measurement performed in the authors’ laboratory.

articleTitle: Implementation of LiDAR and Photogrammetry in Right of Way Assessment for Improving Transmission Line Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The transmission line is the backbone of electrical energy transfer. The reliability of the transmission line is influenced by the condition of the right-of-way path. Currently, the method used to assess the condition of the transmission tower and its ROW is done manually by ground patrol officers equipped with the Srintami application, which must be filled out along with photo evidence of the condition of each item of equipment being assessed. The level of accuracy achieved by using this method is highly dependent on the perceptions of officers and is prone to errors in providing information, so it will affect the results of the assessment and does not comprehensively describe the real conditions in the field. As the development of UAV technology is increasing rapidly, it is possible to apply the use of UAVs for mapping so that the problems that arise in the mapping of ground patrol officers, such as extreme terrain conditions, are no longer a problem. There are two methods of mapping UAVs based on the type of payload used. The first is photogrammetry, which utilizes the camera from the UAV, and the second is using the LiDAR sensor. In photogrammetry, the image results are then processed into a series of photos that are assembled into a 2D map that describes the actual conditions of the transmission line, while in LiDAR, the results of image processing can be in the form of a 3D map, which can directly analyze the distance between the stand and the tower. By combining these two pieces of information, the accuracy of the transmission line conditions becomes more accurate, so that more careful planning can be carried out regarding maintenance that can maintain the reliability of the transmission line.

articleTitle: Surface Partial Discharge Phenomenon at Cable Termination in Medium Voltage Cubicle and Low Voltage Side Box of Power Transformer at PLN West Java Transmission Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Cable termination is a workmanship activity with results depending on how good the worker is to make proper termination. Poor workmanship causes defects that initiate more electric stress and slowly break the dielectric material. Partial discharge (PD) is one of dielectric deterioration symptoms that can be measured in an energized state. Improper cable termination can bring out PD spread locally from its source to the air in the form of an ultrasonic signal called surface PD. PD would cause root tracking pattern in the power cable surface and when it reaches the ground side discharge would occur and would cause failure or breakdown. This paper discussed how to determine cable termination conditions in incoming cubicle and at low voltage side (LV) box of transformers. Contact probe and flexible microphone sensor can detect ultrasonic signals from closed areas. The surface PD signal would travel to the air and creep to the metal surface of the cubicle and LV side box that can be detected with a contact probe. With the same principle, the surface PD travels to the air going out from the air gap of the box and can be detected with a flexible microphone. The decision of any PD detection depends on ultrasonic signal from acoustic emissions and Phase Resolved Partial Discharge (PRPD) pattern with two clusters. In cases from Depok Baru and Ciledug Substation, PD signals are found inside of box compartment. At Depok Baru Substation, PD source from LV side box of transformer detected at Depok substation and exfoliated termination found. At Ciledug Substation, cable terminations visual seen proper workmanship, but to verify which cable that have PD source, corona camera is used. This measurement can become an early warning that initiates corrective action to prevent any failure or material breakdown from hidden assets in the box.

articleTitle: Typical Values of Gas Concentration and Gas Rates Increase in Dissolved Gas Analysis for Power Transformers with Different Operating Voltages
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is a method that is often used in transformer maintenance. Therefore, the interpretation of the results of the gas content in transformer oil must be carried out properly to get the right information regarding the condition of the transformer. The international standards for the interpretation of DGA in transformers with mineral oil are IEEE C57.104 and IEC 60599. In previous research, a comparison of these standards was carried out to find out which typical values from those standards are more in line with the actual conditions of the power transformer. In this research, a typical value of the gas concentration in transformer oil was searched to get better accuracy than typical values in international standards. A total of 6092 samples of transformer mineral oil from 2473 transformer units were used to find typical values of gas concentrations with operating voltage which were divided into several categories, namely category O with > 500kV with subcategory 500 and 525 kV, category A with a voltage rating between 170 kV and 400 kV with subcategory 275 kV, category B with a rated voltage between 72.5 kV and 170 kV with sub-categories of 150 kV and others, and category C with rated voltages between below 72.5 kV with sub-categories of 70 kV, 20kV, and others. In this study, the typical value for individual gas rates was also searched with 765 samples from 500 transformer units. The search for typical values in this study uses the 90 and 95 percentile methods. Typical value from this study will be compared with actual data from 50 transformers. The results are typical values in this study that have better accuracy than typical values in IEC 60599 and IEEE C57.104.

articleTitle: Determination of Weighting Factor for High Voltage Equipment Replacement Priority Index using Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: PLN has regulations for equipment replacement but it should be improved to determine the criticality and priority level of equipment to be replaced. The large amount of equipment meets the replacement criteria has to be prioritized based on risk and impact. In the previous studies, there were discussions in terms of the Analytical Hierarchy Process method to determine the weighting of the parameters that make up the Health Index of the equipment. However, to determine the priority for High Voltage equipment replacement should consider the Risk parameters and Asset Health Index which including Condition Assessment Factor and Performance Assessment Factor. Additionally, the hierarchical model was formed by getting advices from 30 experts which were given a survey to get the weighting of each parameter. These experts have previously been examined in terms of their knowledge and experience, so dependable results can be obtained. The priority for replacing equipment from this research has been running from 2020 to 2022 and had the impact in reducing the number of interruptions and breakdown of equipment.

articleTitle: Power Quality Control Strategy of MMC Inverter as Solid State Transformer on Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The massive penetration of EV, rooftop PV and other power electronic-based loads will be a challenge in the distribution network. Even though conventional transformers are equipped with voltage regulators, they are passive towards harmonics, power quality problems (sag, swell) and reverse power flow due to future distribution network loads. One of the solutions currently being developed is the solid state transformer (SST). This research will focus on the LV stage SST using Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) topology. MMC was chosen as the inverter topology because it provides the most features. The MMC topology provides a feasible and cost-effective approach for a DC/AC converter with a very high number of levels. MMC can control active/reactive power independently and easily control the magnitude, phase and frequency of the AC voltage. The most attractive feature is modularity. The two main control schemes Nearest Level Control (NLC) and Voltage-Frequency Control (VFC) are used as converter control algorithms in the designed MMC inverter. The results of the SST model simulation, the built MMC inverter can transmit and absorb reactive power. MMC inverter can maintain the voltage back to steady state when sag and swell events occur.

articleTitle: Could Economic Dispatch and Unit Commitment with Emission Constraints Reduce Power System Costs? A Case Study on Java-Madura-Bali Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Net Zero Emissions in 2060 has become Indonesia’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions. Reducing emissions from coal-fired power plants is considered a strategic target implemented through a carbon tax. However, the application of a relatively low carbon tax makes the benefits of limiting emissions insignificant. One alternative that has emerged is the deactivation of the coal-fired power plant and its substitution with other low-emission power plants. The problem then arises of calculating the generating capacity of a coal-fired power plant substitution so that the emission reduction target can be achieved while taking into account the reliability and economic criteria of the generator operation. This paper presents research on calculating the generating capacity of a coal-fired power plant substitution with two emission reduction scenarios under normal conditions. Based on the research results, to achieve the emission reduction target of 2.5% and 5% against normal conditions in Java-Madura-Bali, it is necessary to reduce the capacity of coal-fired power plants by 480 MW and 995 MW. In addition, reducing emissions has increased operational costs by IDR 18.4 billion and IDR 90.1 billion per week. The method proposed in this study is considered practical and realistic because it has considered the reliability and economic criteria of system operation. Not only did the simulations with the jROS software, but PT PLN UIP2B JAMALI also implemented this method in the Java-Madura-Bali system on 12 and 13 February 2022. The implementation of this method reduces 9,958 Tons of carbon emissions. However, there was an increase of IDR 34.7 billion in operational costs.

articleTitle: Analysis of Partial Discharge Pulse-sequence Pattern in Air Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) is a discharge phenomenon that occurs locally because of which the insulation and the conductor are partially connected. This work observes and analyzes the character of partial discharges in air insulation. The sensor used in this measurement is the RC Detector. The sensor will measure and forward the PD signal which will be read on the oscilloscope. The results of background noise measurements at amplitudes V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>=140mV, and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf>=-20mV with the RC detector sensor. The PD signal can be analyzed in terms of the PD pulse sequence pattern (PD PSA) where PD occurs. Observations occurred in 50 cycles with three voltage levels of 3.5 kV, 4.0kV, and 4.5 kV respectively. The measurement and analysis results are that the PD will be more numerous and of greater magnitude as the applied voltage increases.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Total Acid Number (TAN) of Synthetic Ester Retrofilled Oil and its Correlation with FTIR Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Retrofilling of an existing mineral oil-immersed transformer with ester oil is an alternative approach to extend the lifespan of transformers. This is associated with the excellent properties of ester oil that has high tolerance to moisture that promotes an advantage to prolong the life of paper insulation. However, the retrofilling process will mix the fresh ester oil with the remaining aged mineral oil in the transformer oil, and eventually affects the performance of the new ester oil. Therefore, it is essential to access the performance of mixed oil in order to detect any signs of oil degradation as a result of retrofilling, prior to transformer energization. In this paper, the total acid number (TAN) and Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectra were measured and analyzed to assess the condition of mixed aged mineral-synthetic ester oil (AMO/SE). Three different proportions of aged mineral oil (AMO), i.e. 3 %, 5 % and 7 % were prepared to simulate different amount of mineral oil residue in a transformer before being retrofilled with fresh synthetic ester oil. The AMO were prepared through thermally ageing of fresh mineral oil in a vacuum oven at 130°C for 150 hours. Based on the findings, it has been intriguingly discovered that the acid number of the AMO/SE oil has decreased as the percentage of AMO increased in fresh synthetic ester oil. In correlation with FTIR spectra, the present acid concentration of the degradation by-product of the retrofilled AMO/SE oils can be observed in carbonyl stretch region at the wavelength of 1700 – 1800 cm$^{-1}$.

articleTitle: Insulator Coating To Improve Outdoor Insulator Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Disturbance to outdoor insulators is caused by several factors and is generally caused by external factors, namely environmental factors. These environmental factors greatly affect the performance of insulators. To improve the performance of insulators, several attempts have been made, such as the use of new materials or surface coatings to increase the dielectric strength. Systematic efforts to improve insulator performance require an understanding of insulator behavior. Most of outdoor insulator failures occur on the surface. Therefore, efforts to improve the performance of outdoor insulators are focused on improving the insulator surface by applying surface treatments or coatings. In this paper, we review research papers that discuss insulator coating materials which results is better performance compared to the uncoated insulator. In this paper, we also propose local material for insulator coating, gum rosin, which is a residue from the distillation of pine tree sap. This product has characteristics namely hydrophobicity, adhesive promoter and viscosity so that it can be used as insulator coating. The final results of this study are expected to contribute to the improvement of insulator performance through insulator coatings. Finally, this insulator coating model can answer the needs of insulators in reduce in a failure problem of outdoor ceramic insulators and experiments were carried out using specimens that had been coated with gum rosin, the result was that the leakage current was reduced.

articleTitle: Modeling of Corona Discharges for High-Voltage Applications in Active Ionic Wind Cooling of High-Power LEDs Lighting
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Ionic wind generation is a good candidate for cooling high power LED lights because it is both quiet, with no moving mechanical parts and very energy efficient. This preliminary work relates to a simulation of the corona discharge of a wire and two plates in air under atmospheric pressure. The results for the same structure are compared with previously published experimental work for ionic wind and temperature and are in good agreement. The use of a narrow diameter wire which achieves a positive corona discharge in air leads to the base plate of an electrode is shown. Hydrodynamics and electrostatics are taken into account in this model. The simulation presented concerns steady-state regimes with the discharge maintained with 9 kV applied to the inner electrode while the outer electrode is grounded. The inconvenient is the lack of a rigorous comparison with experimental airflow, air velocity and current-voltage result. These results are important because they are used as a method of cooling the heat sink of the high-power light-emitting diode, as verified in this work, and also to develop this effect for practical purposes. The dependence of the cooling efficiency on the distance between the plates and the wire was studied.

articleTitle: Effectiveness Verification of the Dynamic Volt-VAR Control to Reduce SVC Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The use of high-penetration solar photovoltaics (PV) to transmission networks is complicated by voltage rise. Infractions of voltage occur when voltage levels surpass the permitted limits. Several solutions have been suggested to avoid voltage breaches, including volt-VAR control on inverters. In this research, the impact of utilizing dynamic volt-VAR control as opposed to static volt-VAR control in a high-penetration photovoltaic (PV) system is compared to the impact of applying static VAR compensator (SVC). With dynamic volt-VAR control, which takes into account the inverter’s available reactive power capacity, it is possible to adjust the reactive power contribution of the PV inverter. The quantity of available capacity will affect the force of the control, as expressed by the droop gain. The transmission system’s controls are evaluated for one year to determine the number of uncompensated voltage occurrences. The number of violations that the control cannot compensate for affects how much reactive power the SVC must provide.

articleTitle: Modeling PV-Wind-Battery Hybrid System for Guest House in Matakus Island
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind energy, present a practical option for fulfilling the electricity generation needs, particularly in areas without electricity access, like Matakus Island. This island has significant potential for utilizing renewable energy, particularly solar and wind energy, due to its coastal location. With an average Global Horizontal Irradiation (GHI) of 6.03 kWh/m2/day and an average wind speed of 6.3 m/s, Matakus Island is well-suited for utilizing these resources. To assess the stability of the proposed Hybrid Power Plant system, modeling is conducted using MATLAB/Simulink. These software tools allow for the evaluation and simulation of the system’s performance under various conditions, ensuring its stability and reliability. The economic analysis of the hybrid power plant is carried out using HOMER Pro, which aids in determining the overall cost-effectiveness of the system. It optimizes the configuration by considering components such as PV panels, wind turbines, batteries, and diesel generators, to find the most economically efficient setup for the hybrid power plant. The electrical system, consisting of an 18.7 kW PV system, a 3kW wind turbine, and a 54 kWh battery, has a Cost of Energy (COE) of Rp. 7,467/kWh, achieves a 100% Renewable Fraction (RF), and results in total annual savings of Rp. 38.1 million. In contrast, relying solely on pure diesel generators leads to a higher COE of Rp. 10,990/kWh, a 0% RF, and generates CO2 emissions of 16, 75Skg/year. The COE using the PV-Wind-battery hybrid system is 32% cheaper than using a diesel generator, demonstrating the significant cost advantage of the hybrid system.
