By implementing a hybrid power plant that combines solar and wind energy with battery storage, Matakus Island can achieve stable and cost-effective electricity generation. This transition to renewable energy not only reduces reliance on expensive and polluting diesel generators but also contributes to a cleaner and more sustainable energy supply.

articleTitle: Design and Testing PCB Rogowski Coil for Lightning Current Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Telecommunication towers and other high-rise buildings are particularly susceptible to lightning strikes. By installing an appropriate lightning protection system, the effects of lightning strikes on telecommunications towers are reduced. Based on observed local lightning characteristics, especially lightning peak current, the lightning protection system is created. In order to validate and monitor the distribution of lightning current that goes through the legs of the tower and down conductors, a suitable lightning current measurement instrument is required. In this study, a measuring instrument based on Rogowski coil was chosen because it has a wide linearity and frequency range which can measure the nature of surges which have a wide frequency and high current. The performance of the designed measuring instrument is tested and calibrated in the laboratory whether it can measure the signal from the surge properly or not. The Rogowski Coil was designed to measure the lightning current up to 100 kA. The novelty of this study is to design Rogowski coil based on local lightning condition that has a good response in low frequency impulse signal.

articleTitle: Health Index Analysis for Electronic And Mechanical Equipment at The Airport
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The asset management is one important point for realibility operation in the airport. In this research, measure the health condition of an equipment asset can be used to provide a mathematical model as basis in support equipment maintenance and equipment replacement strategies. The health condition is calculating in the health index, whilst the methodology used to calculate health index is doing by considering the age of the equipment. When the equipment approach its end of the lifetime, the possibility of failure will increase. However the health index of an equipment is also influenced by location, operating stress and maintenance strategy. All these factors produce an index that shows the speed of equipment aging as define as aging rate. In the case study, the Health Index analysis was carried out for electrical and mechanical equipment at 19 airports under management of Angkasa Pura II. The health index analysis will be base for maintenance classes and decision recommendations for maintenance or replacement equipment in all the airports under management of Angkasa Pura II.

articleTitle: Power Enhancement Analysis from Exhaust Energy Flow of An Open Cycle Gas Turbine Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Optimizing the use of natural gas to reduce fossil fuel consumption can be realized by increasing power output through the utilization of gas turbine exhaust energy. This research presents a power enhancement analysis using the exhaust energy flow of the 30 MW open-cycle gas turbine power plant. The initiative is based on the working principle that opencycle gas turbines generally have an efficiency of 25-30%, which means that up to 70% of energy is directly released into the atmosphere. The analysis uses mass balance calculation of fuel and air supply to find the exhaust energy flow-nevertheless, the modeling simulation of the combined cycle uses the cycle tempo program. The result shows approximately 51.99 MW of energy flow from the gas turbine exhaust. The combined cycle modeling simulation shows that the possibility of improvement is around 13.03 MW or the equivalent of 42.86% power enhancement. This finding indicates that natural gas consumption can be further optimized using a combined cycle rather than a conventional open-cycle gas turbine to reduce energy losses in gas turbine power plants.

articleTitle: Adding of SiO2 Nanocomposite on Insulation Properties for Epoxy Resin Insulating Material
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Insulator is a component that has a very important role in the electrical energy system. The insulator functions as a separator between a conductor and the part that has no voltage. Currently, polymer insulators have been developing, one of which is epoxy resin polymer material. The quality of the epoxy resin insulator is influenced by the mixture of manufacturing materials and filler. This paper discusses the effect of adding of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> filler onthe quality of epoxy resin insulator. Epoxy resin insulator material testing was carried out at high voltage laboratory using an AC Voltage of 3,5 kV 50Hz. The epoxy resin insulator materials tested in this study by adding SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The observed electrical parameter is the leakage current. The contact angle is an observed physical parameter and the degradation time of the insulator surface. The result showed that the addition of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to the epoxy resin reduced the value of the leakage current, degradation time and increased the contact angle.

articleTitle: Design of Moving Wireless Charger for EV Prototype with Inductive Power Transfer Method
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In this paper, the prototype of Moving Wireless Charging for Electric Vehicle will be designed. The Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) method that will be used in this study is the Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) system. The designed WPT system consists of an AC Voltage Source, Transmitter Rectifier, Inverter, LCC Compensation Circuit, Transmitter Coil arrangement, Receiver Coil, Receiver Rectifier, and battery load. In the test related to dynamic charging, the most optimal results were obtained when the distance between the coils was 2 cm with an efficiency of 10.02%.

articleTitle: Naïve Bayes Model for Combining Results from Multi-Methods Fault Identification of Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This research paper presents a development of a Naive Bayes model to combine the results of multi-methods fault identification in power transformers based on dissolved gas analysis (DGA). The proposed model incorporates four commonly used DGA methods: IEC Ratio Method, Rogers’ Ratio Method, Duval Pentagon Method, and Duval Triangle Method. The model uses the results from each method as input features and predicts the presence of fault types in power transformers. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, a dataset containing DGA data with known actual fault from power transformers was used. The results indicate that the simple majority vote increase the accuracy of prediction compared to single method. This approach is easy to implement. However, by using proposed naive bayes model, the increase in accuracy is more pronounced. Overall, the proposed Naïve Bayes model provides a promising approach for combining multi-method fault identification in power transformers based on DGA. The model has the potential to improve the accuracy and reliability of fault diagnosis and facilitate proactive maintenance of power transformers.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Testing of Bow-tie and Long Bow-tie Combination Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Insulation damage is a major cause of high voltage equipment failure. Partial discharge conditions can be used to diagnose insulation conditions in high voltage apparatus. UHF sensors such as bow-tie antennas can detect the EM waves generated when a partial discharge occurs. In order to increase the bandwidth of the antenna, a combination of bow-tie and long bow-tie antennas is investigated. From the simulation results, the combination antenna has a greater bandwidth than the individual antenna with a bandwidth of 1054.5 MHz. In this study the combination antenna was printed and then tested directly in the laboratory. Based on the measurement results for the combination antenna by using the Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), at resonant frequency the combination antenna has a return loss of −34.6793dB, the bandwidth of 441.1018 MHz. The combination antenna shows higher sensitivity than individual antennas in detecting partial discharges directly in the GIS model as seen from the results of the partial discharge pattern and pulse sequence of partial discharge.

articleTitle: Design and Power Quality Performance on Development Bay Capacitor 20 kV-20 MVAR
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Enhancement use of inductive equipment such as the use of motors, transformers, in general the power factor system will decrease, therefore it needs to be compensated by using capacitors. Capacitor on a 20 kV system to reduce reactive energy so that the power factor becomes better. In the current system conditions total capacitor is 12 unit (each capacitor is 40 $\mu \mathrm{F}$, 13857V) for 20 kV-20 MVAR with installed 4-steps system. One step is consist for three phase which can be energized from breaker which triggered by 3 phase power factor sensor. This system 12 unit capacitor was developed into 12 steps (total capacitor still 20 MVAR) with sensors in each phase. From simulation 3-phase unbalanced linear load, it is found that the 12-step system drops 4,75 kW from the conventional system with R123:100$\Omega$, L1:50 mH, L2:20 mH, L3:500 mH. From nonlinear loads simulation, the power factor can be increased and some harmonic and ripple factor can be decreased.

articleTitle: Improving Transmission Reliability and Reducing Cost of Supply in Bangka Island through Sumatra-Bangka Interconnection: A Contingency Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In the distribution of electric power, the issue of distribution reliability is a very significant influence on the continuity of electricity distribution to the customer. Currently, Bangka Island’s electricity system is still dominated by diesel-fueled generators, resulting in the BPP (Cost of Supply) of the electric power system in the area being expensive. The Sumatra system in 2022 will experience a surplus of generation and there are many cheap generators, especially PLTU, so the Sumatra - Bangka interconnection option is something that must be done to reduce the BPP Bangka. The contingency analysis is conducted to evaluate the system’s ability to continue operating in the event of an unexpected failure or outage. The analysis considers various scenarios such as the loss of a generator, or transmission line. The results of the contingency analysis provide valuable information for system operators to develop effective contingency plans and make informed decisions during emergency situations. The study utilizes a combination of analytical and simulation methods to evaluate the system’s performance under normal and contingency conditions. The simulation model is developed using the power system simulation software to simulate various operating scenarios and contingencies. The analysis considers the system’s frequency response, voltage stability, and power flow characteristics. The findings of the study indicate that the Sumatra-Bangka system is highly interconnected, which makes it vulnerable to cascading failures. However, the system’s contingency analysis shows that it can withstand various contingencies with the proper contingency plans and procedures in place. The study recommends that system operators continue to monitor and evaluate the system’s performance regularly and develop contingency plans to maintain the stability and reliability of the power supply to the region.

articleTitle: Discrete Fourier Transform and Correlation Analysis on Highly Penetrated Variable Renewable Energy System to Achieve Frequency Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Renewable energy has been emerging due to global needs. However, the renewable energy power plant’s active power fluctuation will affect the frequency deviation signal. This paper presents a method to reduce frequency fluctuation using Discrete Fourier Transform and Correlation analysis. From the initial simulation, the frequency deviation signal exceeds the limit $(\pm 0.2$ Hz) obtained by conducting the quasi-dynamic analysis due to the fluctuation of solar plant and wind turbine generators. The quasi-dynamic analysis is also compared to the RMS analysis in terms of better time efficiency while simulating the frequency deviation of the system due to the fluctuation of the intermittent power plants. This paper uses a mathematical analysis approach by transforming the time domain signal to the frequency domain signal using Discrete Fourier Transform. The Discrete Fourier Transform transforms the time domain signal of the solar irradiation, wind speed, and frequency deviation signals in a day into the frequency domain signal. The filtered solar irradiation and the wind speed signals by Discrete Fourier Transform then become new inputs and will yield a new frequency deviation signal with less fluctuation and does not exceed the limit. On the other hand, correlation analysis provides the variable renewable energy plants with the most intermittent than others and yield fluctuating frequency deviation violating the limit at the end of the day. The battery energy storage system will compensate for the power fluctuation because of the intermittent power plants to achieve frequency stability.

articleTitle: Post-Seismic Fault Detection and Diagnosis on Power Transformer: A Comprehensive Review and Study Case of Cianjur Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: A power transformer is a vital component in an electrical network system because of its key role in the power system. Guaranteeing transformer continuity and operability in all environmental conditions has emerged as a major topic in transformer fault detection and diagnosis, particularly considering large seismic events that have grown widespread all over the world, with notable ones including Cianjur Earthquake in West Java, Indonesia in 2022. Different approaches for transformer diagnostics are discussed in this research. Along with other diagnostic techniques, SFRA is recognized as one of the most appropriate techniques to identify faults or deformations in power transformers. From the results and analysis of the turn ratio test, it can be concluded that there is no short-circuit in the winding, while in the tan delta, DC insulation resistance, and breakdown voltage tests it can be concluded that there are no significant contaminants in the insulation. From the results of the OLTC dynamic resistance test, it can be concluded that there is no open circuit in the windings at each tap, and there are no defects in the diverter switch or in the OLTC mechanical parts in general. On the other hand, the SFRA test results concluded that there were indications of inter-disk faults and dielectric leakage currents on windings, also residual magnetism or slight deformation in the transformer core. However, the degree of deterioration that occurred was relatively mild and still within the permissible standard limits, so that all four transformers at the Cianjur substation were still usable and operating well today, which had been 6 months after the earthquake.

articleTitle: Optimization and Study of Grid Impact on Photovoltaic Installation — Connected 785 MVA Steam Turbine Power Plant for Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Increased solar integration as a variable renewable energy (VRE) brings many benefits and challenges, especially in typical industrial grids. This paper introduces a methodology to find the optimum installation and operational points for PV by considering several constraints such as generation limitation, spinning reserve, and steam demand to meet plant process operating requirements. In this paper, an analysis will be conducted to investigate the intermittent of renewable energy on the security and stability of the power system with several options for solar capacity. The modeling and simulation of S steam turbine generators and PV will be performed using PowerFactory Digsilent, a power system software that offers various solutions for power system analysis and simulation. Meanwhile the study of UCED is also carried out using solver to analyze actual power measurement data from power plants, based on the integration of variable renewables. The research findings indicate that the optimal installation of up to 50 MWp of solar panels can be achieved gradually, while considering constraints such as spinning reserve equivalent to the largest generator and the system’s ability to handle high-power equipment starting, if required.

articleTitle: Study of Stochastic Approach to Determine Value of Lost Load in Jawa-Madura-Bali System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Jawa-Madura-Bali (JMB) electric power system is the largest electric power system in Indonesia, consuming more than 75% of the total power demand across the country. Therefore, most of the electric consumers in this region expect higher reliability than other areas in Indonesia. However, the national government applies a flat and uniform electrical tariff to the consumers. To justify any investment that satisfies higher reliability expectations, an indicator that defines reliability and financial measure is needed, namely the Value of Lost Load (VoLL). The calculation of VoLL has been conducted through different approaches and methods. This paper compares the approaches and methods of VoLL considering the availability of data and its role to justify the economic feasibility of new investments. The final recommendation for VoLL calculation was conducted on JMB electric power system using the Monte-Carlo approach to satisfy several uncertainty parameters.

articleTitle: Lifetime Study of Transformer 150KV Gas and Steam Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformer BAT.12 PLTGU Priok is a power transformer which has an important role in distributing electrical power from PLTGU Priok to the load network. BAT 12 transformer which has been operating for a long time will certainly experience a decrease in standard and quality due to electrical, thermal, mechanical, chemical, and aging factors. One of the decreases in the standard and quality of the transformer is the decrease in the quality of the winding insulation. During the last two years of operation, there were several disturbances in the BAT. 12 PLTGU Priok transformer. Based on the Maximo 201819647 work order, there is a disturbance that can damage the isolation on the transformer. To determine the condition of the isolation quality and anticipate unexpected transformer breakdowns, it is necessary to test the transformer standard parameters. This test includes testing the insulation quality of the transformer windings. The Tangent Delta, Insulation Resistance and Dielectric Frekeuncy Respone test methods were carried out to determine the standard parameters of the dissipation factor, insulation resistance, polarity index, moisture content and oil conductivity. The test results are Tangent Delta of <0.5%, Oil conductivity of <6.7 pS / m, moisture content of <1.5%, HV / LV Insulation Resistance of 538 MΩ and polarity index of 2.76. The results of this test show that the transformer is still in good condition.

articleTitle: Implementation of Adjustable Adapter Yoke Tool for Live Line Maintenance of Transmission 275 kV and 150 KV Tension Insulator
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transmission and Load Dispatch Center Of Sumatera (UIP3BS) distributes electricity, one of which is through High Voltage Air Over Head Lines (SUTT 150 kV) and Extra High Voltage Air Over Head Lines (SUTET) 275 kV with 63S MW of power of radial system conditions distributed through Sumatra SUTET 275 kV Sumatra network configuration has a system vulnerability map at N-1. The problem occurs due to maintenance by turning off one of the conductors. There is a potential for widespread disruption due to open looping on the 275 kV SUTET segment which can occur because of the failure or problem on one of the maintenance lines and other line interference. However, some double tension insulators were found to break and flash over. Insulator replacement could not be carried out on a live line because the design and dimensions of the cold end yoke adapter did not match 6 types of designs and dimensions of the existing yoke on SUTET 275 kVUIP3B Sumatra. To solve these problems, the Live Line Maintenance (PDKB) UIP3B Sumatera UPT Padang team conducted problem identification and problem-solving analysis. They made an innovation called Adjustable Adapter Yoke. Adjustable Adapter Yoke is an auxiliary equipment in the maintenance of the double tension insulator SUTET 275 kV, functions as a cold end yoke support that can be implemented in various designs and dimensions of the existing yoke with 7075 aluminum dural material. ADJUSTABLE ADAPTER YOKE can be implemented in all types of the existing yokes, in which the replacement of double tension insulators 275 kV and 150 kV can be performed without blackout.

articleTitle: Improvement of Transmission Line Grounding System using Conductive Cement
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Lightning is a natural phenomenon that cannot be avoided, lightning can strike anywhere and anytime depending on the situation and environmental conditions. Lightning has been the biggest caused of transmission faults in most PLN transmission units over the past few years. Transmission line is easy to be struck by lightning, because of its high position and being in an open space. If transmission line grounding system functions properly, the over voltage caused by lightning strikes can be earthing to the ground easily, without causing traveling wave. However, if earthing cannot distribute badly, it can cause transmission fault. Improving transmission line grounding system besides using a good grounding connection from top to bottom grounding, we need to check also properly to ensure a good bottom grounding resistance value, especially in soils with high resistance such as rocky areas. Conductive cement is one of the solutions to improve the transmission line grounding system by replacing the surrounding soil with a low resistance cement. In its implementation, conductive cement can use with ground rod or ground plate and must be well calculated. For ground rod, the influencing factors are diameter of ground rod, diameter of hole, number of rods and spacing between rods. As for the ground plate is plate depth, plate diameter and plate dimensions. Monitoring the implementation of conductive cement that has been implemented using the parameters above shows good results, where using conductive cement with a ground rod can reduce the value of grounding resistance by up to 93% and using a ground plate can decrease by up to 85%. From routine monitoring every month, the value of the grounding resistance is stable until the 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> month, which has passed the rainy and dry season, so that it can be concluded that conductive cement is effective to improving the transmission line grounding system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Co-firing in 25 MW CFB Boiler Coal-fired Power Plant Using Palm Kernel Shell to Support Indonesia Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: By 2025, Indonesia intends to use 23% renewable energy, and by 2060, it wants to be fossil fuel free. One of PT PLN’s (Persero) plans for accelerating carbon emission reduction and expanding the country’s mix of new renewable energy sources is biomass co-firing. To study the technical, financial, and environmental effects connected with the operating parameters, this research provides a methodology for assessing the performance of biomass co-firing applied in a coal-fired power plant. The palm kernel shell (PKS), which has the highest biomass potential nearby (Sumatra Island), is being used in the biomass co-firing process at the 25 MW coal-fired power plant (CFB type boiler). The main steam temperature, pressure, and flow value are within a normal range, according to the combustion test from 0% to 100% co-firing ratio. Co-firing with more PKS will minimize emissions from coal-fired power plants, especially Nitrogen Oxide (NN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>), Sulfur Dioxide (OS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), and carbon dioxide (OC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) avoided by burning biomass. A PKS for biomass co-firing will also demonstrate a decrease in production cost-effectiveness based on the Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) value. The development and use of biomass co-firing would enhance Indonesia’s energy transition toward 2060 Net Zero Emissions thanks to the suggested methodology for performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Reducing Partial Discharge Activity in a Large Generator Unit by Increasing Hydrogen (H2) Pressure
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: There are several coal-fired power plants in Indonesia. Typically, this power generation district consists of some generator units with a capacity of several thousand MW. Generators with large capacities are generally hydrogen-cooled, water-cooled, or a combination of both. One of the problems that occur in a generator is the high partial discharge (PD) activity at several areas within the stator part. The phenomenon of partial discharge can be recorded by the coupling capacitor sensor and the Resistance Temperature Detector (RTD) Module assembled into one monitoring equipment. The Coupling Capacitor function is to detect partial discharge for each phase, while the RTD module function is as a partial discharge detector through radio frequency and correlates it with temperature and humidity data in a wide range of sensing and spreads throughout the generator winding area. This paper describes the Partial Discharge in the hydrogen-cooled generator and how to reduce the Partial Discharge activity. Hydrogen pressure effects on the Partial Discharge activity were investigated. Partial discharge activity is observed in the form of point of view magnitude and pulse per cycle (PPC) by varying the pressure. Increasing the pressure is taken as a mitigation step so that the generator can operate continuously until the time for rewinding comes. It was found that partial discharge activity reduced significantly as the hydrogen pressure on the generator is increased from the nominal pressure. The Partial Discharge Intensity value can decrease from 250 milliwatts to around 160 milliwatts at a pressure of 0.35 MPa and can even decrease to an average value of 120 milliwatts at a pressure of 0.4 MPa This phenomenon was explained by using the increasing of Partial Discharge inception according to Paschen Law for hydrogen.

articleTitle: Finite Control Sets Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) Implementation in PV Converter System for Maintaining The DC Bus Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) panels are becoming increasingly attractive for use in DC microgrids as they are one of the Renewable Energy Source (RES) harvesting devices that are becoming cheaper. In most cases, the PV system is operated in Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) mode, which extracts the maximum amount of energy in the form of electric current to provide to the microgrid. The converter on the battery system is responsible for the distribution, power-sharing, and stability of the DC bus voltage. Therefore, the battery converter system plays a crucial role, as any disturbance in this system can disrupt the stability of the DC microgrid system and potentially cause it to fail. In addition to extracting maximum sunlight energy, PV systems can also maintain the bus voltage with proper treatment. This ensures that the system remains stable even if the battery system fails for a limited time, provided that solar radiation conditions are sufficient to handle the load. Several methods for maintaining the bus voltage using PV systems have been proposed in the literature. However, the time response of the systems needs improvement to become faster. This paper aims to address this issue by proposing a modifying objective function variable implemented in Finite Control Sets Model Predictive Control (FCS MPC). The objective function is derived from the PV inductor current’s Integral Absolute Error (IAE). In contrast, the current reference is obtained from integrating the PV boost converter’s output voltage error. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through Simulink Matlab simulation, which demonstrates its ability to maintain bus voltage even in the battery system converter is unavailable.

Author Keywords: PV system for DC bus control

articleTitle: Development of Printed Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna as UHF Sensor for Partial Discharge Detection in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) activity in high voltage (HV) and medium voltage (MV) asset is an alarming sign of its insulation deterioration. Ultra-high frequency (UHF) technique, commonly known as the unconventional method, has been widely applied for monitoring the insulation condition of HV and MV apparatuses such as transformers, gas-insulated switchgears (GIS), rotating machines, etc. This UHF method is widely used due to its anti-interference capability, especially for online PD monitoring where electromagnetic interferences such as noise from telecommunication and corona can significantly be mitigated. UHF sensors (antennas) play an integral role in UHF PD monitoring. Many researches on the UHF antennas designs for PD detection on HV or MV power apparatuses have been previously carried out in the literature. However, some UHF sensors developed so far still experience insufficient bandwidth gain, which in turn may result in low sensitivity to PD-induced electromagnetic signals, especially in online PD detection. A new type of UHF antenna called printed rectangular microstrip patch antenna (RMPA) is presented in this paper. This UHF antenna was designed, simulated, and optimized using the HFSS software. The proposed RMPA has a compact size, wide bandwidth and low return loss below −10dB. Upon fabrication of the antenna prototype, the vector network analyzer was used to test the antenna’s performance. In addition, to validate the sensitivity performance of the designed antenna, this antenna was implemented, through laboratory experiments, to capture and measure PD signals emitted by artificial insulation defects in oil insulation. The PD measurement results confirmed that this antenna is suitable for PD monitoring on HV or MV power assets such as oil-insulated transformers.

articleTitle: Implementation of Home Energy Management System for Indonesia Homes with Hybrid Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In this research, model design and system simulation are carried out to determine the feasibility of implementing a hybrid solar power plant (PLTS). Using the Home Energy Management System (HEMS) technology platform will be applied to housing in Indonesia which consists of hardware and software to allow users to monitor energy use and production regularly both conventionally (manually) and automatically (automatically). The goal is not only to assist government programs in implementing regional electricity networks and programs to accelerate the use of electric vehicles, in the form of analysis, design models and system simulations, but we can also find out the feasibility of the HEMS platform and get energy. efficiency gains in Indonesian people’s homes later. By using the Homer Pro software, the design of the Hybrid Solar Power Plant can work to meet the load on the electricity grid. With an average CoE value of IDR 403.00/kWh with an NPC value of IDR. 140,412,000.00 with a return duration of 9.4 years. Then to maximize the Solar Power Plant components, the use of the HEMS platform was implemented using the Matlab Link Dispatch provided by the Homer Pro software, the system behaviour was successfully changed according to the author’s wishes, where the simulation results with Homer Pro software and Matlab software with the lowest purchase limit tested was 50% of the total purchasable grids. Hybrid Solar Power Plant rods can work to meet the needs of the electricity load with an average CoE value of IDR 226.95 /kWh. With an NPC value of IDR 82,205,540.00 with a payback duration of 5.6 years. Yields are influenced by how much and how much of these components are used, then how much energy is purchased from the provider and how much excess is resold.

articleTitle: Application of Non-Linear Discrete Spatial Permittivity Distributions in Reducing Electric Field Concentration in GIS Spacer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This research is focused on investigating the application of electric field grading method of functionally graded material (FGM) on a GIS spacer can reduce the maximum electric field intensity around the GIS triple junction area. To realize this purpose, FGM spacers in this study is using a fabricated discrete technique (stepwise layers). This study uses a spatial distribution model of discrete permittivity ($\varepsilon_{\mathbf{r}}$) of 5 layers with a value of 3.5 to 7.5. The composite filler that is mixed into the Epoxy Resin is TiO$_{\mathbf{2}}$ particles with high permittivity and SiO$_{\mathbf{2}}$ particles with low permittivity. The graded permittivity distribution is expected to allow effective in control the maximum of electric field strength along the surface of the spacer, especially in the triple junction (TJ) area as the weakest pant of the GIS insulation. From the electric field simulation results, it is obtained that permittivity distribution of the U-shape can reduce the electric field intensity around the high voltage triple junction (TJ-HV) area from 399.90 kV/m to 251.34 kV/m with 37% reduction. The large to small permittivity distribution (BS-FGM) can reduce the electric field intensity from 399.90 kV/m to 249.38 kV/m, with 38% the electric field. The final results of this study shows that fabricating spacer with permittivity distribution of Ushape, filler loading weight of 30% is used for the middle layer of the spacer, while part near the TJ-HV and TJ-GND sections, a filler loading weight of 40% is used vs the total weight of the epoxy resin matrix.

articleTitle: I-V Lissajous Pattern: a Promising Condition Monitoring Technique for High Voltage Assets
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of critical high voltage assets such as power transformers, overhead transmission lines and underground cables are affected by various factors including the asset’s health state along with other operating and environmental conditions. Understanding the current-voltage characteristics of such assets is essential for reliable and efficient operation of power transmission and distribution networks. The measurement of such parameters does not call for additional hardware as it utilises easily accessible voltage and current data at both terminals of the asset. The I-V characteristic can be considered as a unique fingerprint for the asset during its normal operation. variations in the fingerprint can be easily detected using a proper software code. The variation can be observed in real time and analysed using digital image processing and artificial intelligence-based techniques to identify and quantify any abnormal event or a fault at early stage. This paper discusses the potential of using the I-V Lissajous pattern to detect incipient faults and abnormal events of high voltage assets. Some case studies on power transformer and overhead transmission line are presented. Results show that I-V Lissajous pattern is a promising technique for real time asset management of high voltage critical equipment.

articleTitle: Inlet Guide Vane Control System Modification to Improve the Reliability of Gas Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Inlet Guide Vane (IGV) is a component in Gas Turbines (GT) that functions as a place for air inflow to the turbine gas compressor. The function of IGV is to maintain an appropriate fuel-to-air ratio in various load of a GT which is related to exhaust temperature, a mandatory operating parameter of a GT operation. In 2020-2021, there were 11 force outages occurred caused by the IGV abnormal position with a total opportunity loss more than 2,789 GWh. The aim of this paper is to modify GT IGV control system to reduce force outages caused by the IGV abnormal position. On existing IGV control system, there is no logic in IGV system that is able to stop the movement of IGV that cause the abnormal position. The modifications were made by adding logic position feedback to the pilot oil pressure of 1 degree up the trip limit of the GT at 45 degrees, so that the GT does not experience a force outage and the GT operator can counteract by setting the GT at a minimum load, which is 70 MW. Based on the results of this paper, in 2022 there was no GT force outages caused by the Inlet Guide Vane abnormal position and there was no opportunity lost obtained. Thus, it can be concluded that the modification of the IGV control system that has been carried out can reduce force outages effectively and improve the reliability of the gas turbine.

articleTitle: AJO (Adjustable Camelong) Conductor Clamp Tool for Repairing Corroded Insulator and String Set Insulators in Transmission Networks and Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transmission and Load Dispatch Center Of Sumatera (UIP3BS) are the units that handle the distribution section of the electricity sector. Electric power is channeled through Transmission and Substations spread across Sumatera Island. The total number of transmissions managed is 28,360 Towers with a total of 208 GI/GITET spread across the Sumatera Island managed by 9 Transmission Implementing Units, 3 Load Control Implementing Units and 1 Sumatera Control Center Unit. Installation growth in Sumatera P3B Main Unit continues to grow with many Transmission and Substation construction projects ongoing. The role of P3B Main Unit is essential to maintain the reliability of installations. For this reason, it is necessary to undergo the maintenance and repair of assets managed by UIP3B Sumatera effectively. Based on field data, there are still many dirty insulators, flash over, and corrosion on insulator string sets that must be repaired immediately. A problem was found when PDKB UPT Padang TEAM carried out maintenance; one of Camelong’s work equipment could not be used on conductors measuring 800 mm2, 1000 mm2, 1200 mm2 and conductors of the HCLS, ACCC, AAAC types. To solve this problem, UPT Padang conducted problem identification and problem-solving analysis by creating an innovation tool. The innovation is AJO (Adjustable Camelong), an equipment for clamping conductors in replacing insulators and string set insulators at transmission and substations. AJO can be used on all sizes of conductors and conductors of the HCLS, ACCC, AAAC types. It can also be used in Live Line and Offline maintenance method.

articleTitle: IEC 61850 Interoperability Testing for SCADA Product Verification
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: IEC 61850 interoperability testing aims to ensure SCADA products can communicate with other products by protocol. This paper discusses the document requirements, preparation, and interoperability testing of IED BCU. The passing criteria are fulfilling all test items (TSD, RCD, TM, testing between IED BCU and GOOSE).

articleTitle: Prediction Health Index Using Machine Learning and Its Correlation with Transformer Age on Historical Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The transformer is a vital of equipment in the power transmission and distribution system. Optimum use of transformers can increase the economic value and reliability of electricity supply. Power apparatus is expected to operate close to or exceed the design life of the transformer. Health index (HI) is used to provide a general assessment of the condition of the transformer. In determining the health index, it can be done using conventional methods or non-conventional methods. According to the IEEE loading guide lines, the age of the transformer ranges from 25-30 years. The “effective age” of the transformer can be determined by the probability of failure of insulation system or which can be based on HI. In this study, transformer oil testing was used to determine the health index and calculate the age of the transformer. The parameters used are BDV, Water, Acid, IFT, DGA, and 2-furaldhyde. In this study, 79 transformer oil sample data were used which had known health indexes from field assessments. The health index method uses calculation, ANN, and naïve Bayes methods. Parameters affecting the health index BDV (r = 0.57), water (r = -0.55), 2FAL (r = -0.58), and acetylene (r = - 0.25). Parameters that affect the life of the transformer are BDV (r = 0.45), water (r = -0.66), Acid (r = -0.53), IFT (r = - 0.49), 2FAL (r = - 0.58), and CO2 (r = -0.40). Parameters BDV, water, and 2 FAL have a significant correlation in determining the health index and predicting the life of the transformer. Parameters 2FAL and water are related to chemical reactions in the insulation system which result in aging of the transformer. With the deteriorating condition of the transformer (HI), it further increases the possibility of initial disturbance to failure of the transformer.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Capacitor Installation by Considering Capacity and Location of Capacitor Optimization in 20 kV Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Power losses are common problems that cause the electricity distribution will not to be optimally delivered. This research aimed to minimize power losses in the 20 kV distribution network by installing capacitors with a case study on the Majenang 06 (MJG06) feeder. It is necessary to do an accurate calculation to get the most optimal capacitor installation results. Calculations are carried out by using the power factor correction diagram method to find the reactive power demand. The reactive power demand at the load center was calculated by the average of its three phases of 600 kVAR. However, a new challenge occurs when the available capacitors in the warehouse are only sized at 300 kVAR per phase. So, two capacitors are required to fulfill the reactive power injection. Furthermore, load flow analysis method is used to search for the optimal combination locations of two capacitors installation is conducted by considering the largest decrease in power losses. This research has been implemented on 20 kV distribution network, and the result shows that the capacitors could raise the average power factor to 0.98 followed by a reduced value of power losses. It proves that this proposed method can improve power quality in the 20 kV distribution network.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Thermal Losses in NH Fuses Among Various Products in the Indonesian Market
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: NH Fuse is one of the main components in PLN’s Low Voltage Connection Panel (PHB-TR). In the PLN electrical system, the NH Fuse is generally installed on the PHB-TR as a safeguard against overloading or overcurrent disturbances. However, the NH Fuse also contributes losses to the electrical system. Electricity utility companies need to reduce network losses, one of which is by selecting components with low losses. In this paper, a comparison of the losses of various brands of NH fuse will be presented using a simple test using nominal current injection (In). Several operating points below the nominal current were also observed to determine the characteristics of losses to increased loading because, in real installations on Low Voltage Sharing Devices (PHB-TR), the NH Fuse is often operated at a load below its nominal current.

articleTitle: Space Charge Accumulation in Thermally Aged Epoxy Resin
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Long-term thermal, electrical, and environmental stresses modifies the material microstructures, causing insulation degradation. One of the indicators of material degradation may be increased space charge accumulation in its volume. In the present paper, space charge distribution within unaged and aged epoxy resin under the DC electric field are studied using the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method. Space charge parameters like apparent trap-controlled mobility and trap depth are estimated, assuming a two-trap level model. Concurrently, chemical changes in the material are identified through the FTIR analysis. Apparent trap control mobility is seen to decrease with aging. Both the shallow and deep trap depths increase with thermal aging.

articleTitle: An Investigation into Measurement Anomaly for Dual-Feeder and Dual Energy Metered Customer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Recently, the electricity market has become more complex because the energy flow is no longer unidirectional to the customers. Hence, a well-designed measurement system is mandatory, not only to measure energy accurately, but also to avoid transaction conflict for the customers. This paper presents the results of an investigation by PLN regarding a customer measurement anomaly in Central Java. The measurement devices recorded unusual energy transferred to and from the customer. The customer was burdened with a huge electricity bill because the customer was not an authorized PLN prosumer. However, there was no evidence that the customer’s internal power plants could generate the recorded amounts of energy. The investigation revealed several factors that contributed to the anomaly. This analysis can aid engineers in designing proper measurement systems, particularly in today’s complex markets with various tariffs and calculations, to prevent similar issues from arising in the future

articleTitle: A Preliminary Result of Lightning Peak Current Measurement in Cilacap at Central Java, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: There is a lot of lightning in Indonesia. Many lightning strike-related incidents have resulted in harm and destruction. Research on lightning peak currents was conducted in the maritime tropical continent region, including Cilacap, in order to limit potential damage in the future. Some cases related tank explosions in Cilacap (Central Java, Indonesia) triggers the research about lightning peak current statistic. According to the statistics, there is a 50% probability of a lightning event that Cilacap will have a lightning peak current of 18 kA. National and international lightning protection standards can be developed using local statistics from this study.

articleTitle: Integrating Existing Pre-Paid Energy Meter to Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) has the capability to calculate system losses in real time, which is a significant advantage. However, this calculation requires the reading of all meters in a cluster, which becomes challenging when independent prepaid meters exist between an AMI meter cluster. These meters are not linked to the AMI system, making it difficult to include them in the calculation of system losses. To address this issue, this study proposes a solution to incorporate pre-existing prepaid meters into the AMI system. The study also includes a gap analysis of the integration process, identifying potential challenges and areas for improvement. In addition, the study conducts laboratory testing to prove the concept. Overall, this study provides a practical solution to a significant challenge in the implementation of AMI technology. The proposed solution can help energy providers to improve their energy management systems, reduce system losses, and enhance their overall energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Off-Grid PV Generation Systems for 3T (Frontier, Outermost, and Least Developed) Regions Using Lead Acid Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesia is an archipelagic state and has various geographical conditions. This situation presents its own challenges for Indonesia in providing reliable electricity for the community, especially for the 3T (Frontier, Outermost, and Least Developed) regions. Off-Grid Solar Power Plant (PLTS) is a popular and rational option for supplying electricity to many of these areas. However, this generation system is intermittent so that if it is operated outside the utility grid, an energy storage device is needed. The most widely used energy storage device is the battery. A relatively inexpensive battery is a lead-acid type battery, but its life cycle is relatively short.

articleTitle: Investigating the potential of renewable energy in the successful energy transition base on hydrology analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The use of fossil fuels occupies the first place of human needs for energy provided by nature, climate change, the extinction of rare animal species, droughts or successive floods are also problems caused by excessive consumption of fossil fuels. This situation requires us to be able to solve it through proper planning using energy modeling tools. This research aims to exploit existing resources to produce new energy sources amid the limitation of old energy sources by producing optimal energy with different sources. Hydrology analysis is carried out to predict the water discharge that will enter the next 5-10 years, with this we can engineer inbound water drainage to produce optimal water depletion and can produce environmentally friendly energy, water flow discharges in the river flow area loss reaches a figure of 6.58 $m^{3}$/sec, which with the flow can be used energy modeling tool such as Mini Hydro Power Plant. According to the results of this investigation, the potential for Pesanggrahan Watershed is more appropriate to be built type Mini Hydro Power Plant with a dependable flow has potential electricity of water power of 405,9 kWatt. And this energy modeling tool can meet the needs of the community energy and also reach Indonesia’s net zero emission (NZE) in the year 2060.

articleTitle: Investigating the Root Causes of Interbus Transformer Breakdowns in Kembangan Substation: lessons learned and recommendations
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Power transformers, designed to transmit electrical power, are key components for the electrical grid and industrial processes, therefore they are one of the most important equipment for electrical energy transfers in a power system. Any failure in transformer leads to malfunction of whole power system. Unfortunately, the impact of the interbus transformer failure at the Kembangan substation is very high, which are energy not served, extra fuel cost, equipment costs and customer satisfaction. The breakdown occurred after energizing for less than 5 days. Previously, the bushing on the interbus transformer had been replaced. Commissioning testing, such as tan delta testing, RDC testing, DGA testing, polarity index testing, and SFRA testing, have been conducted. Before energizing, all test results were assessed and still within PLN’s standard tolerance limits, except for SFRA test results which showed some conditions outside the tolerance limits. This paper discusses a case study that occurred in Kembangan substation on the interbus transformer asset, highlighting the importance of evaluating SFRA test results after performing mechanical treatment on the asset.

articleTitle: Modified Cuk Converter-Based Two-Stage Microinverter Topology Design
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The application of renewable energy in the form of photovoltaics is a challenge to provide electrical energy for people lives in remote areas which in turn will improve their life quality. The proposed modified Cuk converter-based two-stage microinverter topology design that able to directly convert low voltage DC voltage output of single PV panel, DC-DC converter is put as the first stage, while modified Cuk converter works to convert into 220 Vac 50 Hz in the second stage. To anticipate the disturbance due to change of solar irradiance, this paper also proposes closed-loop system to keep the constant 220 Vac 50 Hz output. It can be shown that the proposed topology and control method is successfully generate constant output voltage from single PV panel input under irradiance disturbance conditions.

articleTitle: Study of Protection System Setting to Mitigate Inrush Current Phenomenon: A Case Study in PT PLN (Persero) UPT Durikosambi
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformers are essential components of electric power transmission systems. The reliability of the transformer protection system is crucial to ensuring the continuity of the electric power supply. Inrush current occurs when there is a significant change in voltage on a particular side of the transformer winding, such as when the transformer is switched on. This phenomenon is not a fault, but it can generate enormous currents and, in some cases, cause differential and Restricted Earth Fault (REF) protection to initiate an unnecessary circuit breaker trip. This paper presents a case study of the analysis of transformers protection system setting at PT PLN (Persero) UPT Durikosambi to mitigate the inrush current phenomenon. This paper will analyze the characteristics and behavior of the inrush current phenomenon based on recorded data when an inrush occurs from a protective relay. Furthermore, the implementation of second harmonic blocks in differential and REF transformer protection is discussed. The results showed that this logic function could mitigate the inrush current phenomenon, thereby preventing unnecessary trips and improving the reliability of the differential and REF protection.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Defective Solar PV Module Inspection Using Thermal Infrared and Electroluminescence Imaging Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The demand for renewable energy has led to a rapid increase in the production and installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems worldwide. However, during transportation, installation, and exposure to adverse weather conditions, PV panels are prone to defects that reduce their lifespan and efficiency. Visual and I-V curve test inspection methods are commonly used to maintain the smooth operation of PV systems, but they are limited by the inability to detect most flaws, the need for expertise, and long inspection times. Hence, there is a need for cost-effective and efficient inspection methods to identify defects in solar panels. The objective of this paper is to analyze and compare the benefits and effectiveness of two solar PV inspection methods, namely thermal infrared (IR) imaging and electroluminescence (EL) imaging. Indoor and outdoor IR images are captured using a FLIR Pro thermal camera and EL images are captured using a low-cost converted Panasonic GF3 camera. The results of our study demonstrate that while each method has its advantages, EL imaging is the most effective method for detecting a wide variety of solar cell defects. Thermal IR imaging is useful for detecting defects that affect the temperature of the panel but may not detect minute defects such as microcracks. The simplicity and low-cost nature of the developed EL setup make it a viable option for small and large PV systems, contributing to the advancement of the solar PV inspection field.

articleTitle: Gas Engine Power Plant Configuration Optimization Using Loss of Load Probability and Expected Energy Not Served: An Indonesian Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Selecting a Gas Engine Power Plant (GEPP) configuration during the feasibility study stage has a crucial impact on decision-making to minimize the total cost incurred during the power plant lifetime. The total cost analyzed in this study consists of construction cost and total revenue loss during the operation stage. Indonesian National Electricity Supply Business Plan (RUPTL) document does not mention the specific configuration for GEPP, only defining the total capacity of the planned power plant. A case study was conducted to analyze the optimum 50 MW GEPP configurations using LOLP and EENS analysis in the Papua Region. Probabilistic approaches by Analytical Method and Monte Carlo Simulation were conducted by varying load loss and Forced Outage Rate. By using an analytical method, the 3x17.55 MW GEPP configuration gives the best option at a load below 35 MW if FOR varied from 0.02 to 0.1. The GEPP arrangement with 4x13.65 MW, 5x11 MW, 6x8.78 MW, and 10.55 MW could offer the lowest cost setup at a load above 35 MW, depending on the FOR and the load values. Monte Carlo Simulation also gives similar results for a 3x17.55 MW configuration giving around 80.8% likelihood of the lowest overall total cost. At above 35 MW load, a 4x13.65 MW GEPP has around 43.5% likelihood of having the least cost, while a 3x17.55 MW has around 37.1% probability. Based on the analysis, determining a proper value of load and FOR is required to obtain the least cost GEPP configurations. Further research can be enhanced from this study by conducting a detailed financial analysis which incorporated EENS analysis, to determine the lowest Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) of the proposed GEPP configurations.

articleTitle: Calculation of Minimum Generator Inertia Based on Unit Commitment to Increase Awareness of Stability in the Jawa Bali System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: To deal with the coming of Variable Renewable Energy (VRE) integration in the Java-Bali Power System, the moment of inertia becomes one of the challenges to be considered. The inertia moment is related to the ability of a system to maintain the stability of frequency when a power imbalance occurs in the system. According to that challenge, several factors affect the amount of inertia moment, such as the number and types of generators and the load characteristics connected to the grid. The ability of the system to prevent system collapse is stronger when the inertia is high. In Java-Bali Power System, the stiffness index uses a historical and statistical method in MW/Hz. In this research, another approach to measure the stiffness index is performed. The method calculates the correlation between the moment of inertia and the Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) in Hz/second. Manual computations are used to determine the RoCoF and inertia moment in the system utilizing statistical data from a few previous disturbance events. These calculations will obtain the minimum value of system inertia during peak and off-peak load periods. At the peak load period, the requirement of minimum inertia is 141,768 MVAs, while the off-peak load minimum inertia is 98,931 MVAs. Therefore, those inertia values will become the Dispatcher’s awareness parameter while controlling the real-time operating system.

articleTitle: Modeling Small Signal Analysis Using Kharitonov’s Theorem Case: Inverter Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Microgrid systems are becoming more popular and the main component in a microgrid system is generation, which in a microgrid system usually consists of distributed generations (DGs). Because the renewable energy (RE) generators are an inverter-based generator, a microgrid dominated by RE generators is called inverter-based microgrid. Due to intermittency of RE generator, such as solar PV, the RE power generation variation may cause instability. The conventional method to analyze system stability due to the variation of loads and generation is modal analysis. In this experiment the proposed method for analyzing small signal stability is by using Kharitonov’s Theorem. The objective of this experiment is to analyze inverter-based stability using Kharitonov’s Theorem and compare it to the result using conventional analysis method which is modal analysis. Using Kharitonov’s Theorem, the system stability can be determined for several operation scenarios within certain time range. In this experiment, the inverter-based microgrid will be modeled using DIgSILENT PowerFactory and the system matrices will be exported into MATLAB software to be analyzed and converted to four transfer functions using Kharitonov’s Theorem. The four output transfer function will determined the system small signal stability of modeled microgrid in one day operation.

articleTitle: Leveraging Performance Evaluation through Special Maintenance of Photo Voltaic Power Plant in Nusa Tenggara Region to Achieve Photovoltaic Reliability Excellence
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: PLN committed to achieve renewable energy mixture up to 23% in 2025 that consists of 8.0% water, 7.3% geothermal, 1.8% wind & solar, and 5.8% biomass/waste/co-firing as listed in the 2021-2030 Electricity Procurement Plan (RUPTL) of PLN, as the greenest or environmentally friendly RUPTL with the portion of renewable energy power plants set to 51.6%. To achieve such ambitious target, PLN has developed several Communal Photovoltaic Power Plants either Off-Grid System, On-Grid System and also Hybrid System, scattered across Indonesia especially in the small and remote island in the eastern region of Indonesia. This paper aims to perform novel performance evaluation through specific Mapping and Scanning of main component of Photovoltaic (PV) Power Plant. The scope of performance evaluation focused on main component of PV Power Plant like PV panel, and inverter only. This paper includes lesson-learned and success story of PV Power Plant operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: Repair On Site Internal Transformer’s Damage Case Based on Through Fault Current Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformers breakdown in PLN Unit Induk Transmisi Jawa Bagian Tengah (PLN UIT JBT) from year 2008 until 2019 as much as 56 times. These breakdown classified into three (3) subsystem, there are On Load Tap Changer, Bushing and Active part. Active part damage, especially in winding, are the most major cases happened, as much as 34 from 56 damage (61%), it was almost caused by Through Fault Current (TFC) in Seconday side of transformer. For increasing the reliability power system, enhance predictive maintenance and reduce transformer outage, PLN UIT JBT-UPT Salatiga have been assess 20 from 72 transformer which has been passed over withstand capability (Through fault current calculation) in dangerous classification condition (% ISQT> 100%). There are three power transformer in poor healthy index condition as an early warning damage so then need to be investigated in internal of power transformer. From the result of internal power transformer investigation, two power transformer need to be repaired on site (Minor Overhaul) because of internal anomaly finding such as carbon which attaches to the active parts, broken insulation paper in the lead bushing, burning out (Flashover) within the pressboard, OLTC’s flexible resistor damage, sludge oil contamination and lossening the connector lead bushing secondary, so that these coorective action hopefully can enhance the lifetime of power transformer. The other one power transformer declared as not ready for operating again (shutdown permanently) because of tertiary winding connection break out.

articleTitle: Utilization of Renewable Energy for Charging Station in Indonesia New Appointed Capital City, Nusantara
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesia has a plan to move the capital city from Jakarta to Nusantara in 2045. The government will implement post pandemic development in Nusantara with one of the most important points is decarbonization. The decarbonization is the policy to reduce emission until net zero emission condition is achieved. The decarbonization will be realized by utilization of renewable energy source and pure electric vehicle. Pure electric vehicle may not generate any emission although the emission may come from the electricity source such as coal power plant and diesel power plant. In order to realize decarbonization in electric vehicle application, one of the alternative solutions is providing charging station with renewable energy sources. There are several gas stations in Indonesia have been equipped with charging station including direct charging for vehicle and charging for battery swap station. However, the electricity source still dominated by non-renewable energy sources. In this paper, charging station with renewable energy source is proposed to support decarbonization policy from Indonesia Government especially in new appointed capital city, Nusantara. The renewable potency in Nusantara is discussed and then, based on government plan in developing Nusantara, charging station will be located close to government building area and covered at least 5 km distance similar with gas stations minimum distance requirement in Indonesia. From the simulation, it is known that daily temperature in Nusantara already comply with Standard Test Condition (STC) and annual average of solar Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) around 4.75 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day. However, the annual average wind speed data in Nusantara is only 1.90 m/s. Solar energy is promising although wind power plant is not promising in Nusantara. Simulation results are shown and discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Harmonic Stability in MMC-HVDC Applications Controlled as a Virtual Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Along with the increased requirements of grid-forming assets, a thorough comprehension of the impact of these controls on the system’s harmonic stability gains more and more importance. Therefore, previous research contributed to understanding the admittance-shaping effects of the main control loops related to a converter controlled as a virtual synchronous machine. In extension to previous investigations, this paper focuses on the impact of implementation and design of the ac voltage controller. In light of dynamic performance requirements of power quantities, structural adjustments – namely, a power feed-forward - have been proposed in literature. However, these adjustments might influence the frequency-dependent behavior of modular multilevel converters controlled as a virtual synchronous machine. Therefore, the impact of these dynamics are derived analytically and evaluated by means of their admittance-shaping effects, too. A final summary classifies all admittance-shaping effects of structural and design related dynamics within virtual synchronous machine controlled modular multilevel converters.

Author Keywords: power system control power system stability

articleTitle: Impact of The Increase in Fuel Cost for Jawa Madura Bali Electricity System Due to Carbon Tax Implementation Plan in 2022
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Indonesian Government through Law Number 7 of 2021 Article 13 and Presidential Regulation Number 98 of 2021 will regulate the implementation of a carbon tax as a form of commitment to environmental impacts by imposing a carbon tax rate of Rp30/kg of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The energy sector, especially in coal-fired power plants, is subject to the implementation of this carbon tax. PT PLN (Persero) through the Board of Directors Regulation No. 0161. P/DIR/2021 expressed support for government policies in the effort to transition energy to net zero emissions by 2060. As a leading system operator in Indonesia, PT PLN (Persero) UIP2B Jawa, Madura and Bali have an eventful role in managing generation operations in the Jawa-Bali system dominated by coal-fired power plants with energy production from coal of 150,6 TWh or around 73.83% of the 2022 fuel mix. Within the scope of PLN, PT PLN (Persero) UIP2B Jawa, Madura and Bali produce 204.03 TWh or around 75% of national electricity production in 2022 planning. This paper is intended to analyze the impact of the increase in fuel costs Jawa-Bali electricity system in 2022 on the implementation of the carbon tax scheme which is “Cap and Tax” and Cap and Trade The simulation is carried out using the jROS Application (Joint Resource optimization and Scheduler) on the 2022 yearly operation plan PT PLN (Persero) UIP2B Jawa, Madura and Bali by adding the verified emission factor input from each coal power plant in the Jawa Madura Bali electricity system. The simulation results show the accumulation of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> production from all coal power plants during 2022, with a comparison of the two schemes “Cap and Trade” and “Cap and Tax”, the conclusion is the “Cap and Trade” scheme is more profitable for PT PLN (Persero) with the difference in fuel costs for the Jawa-Bali system of Rp76.57 billion, which is cheaper than “Cap and Tax” scheme.

articleTitle: Review of Transient Earth Voltage Sensor Implementation to Detect Partial Discharge in High Voltage Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper reviews the implementation of a Transient Earth Voltage (TEV) sensor to detect partial discharge in high-voltage equipment. The use of TEV as a partial discharge sensor is one of the main choices recently because of its ease of use. Research regarding the implementation of TEV has been carried out by many researchers. The research conducted is mainly for metal-enclosed high-voltage equipment such as GIS, Transformers, etc. The main purpose of this paper is to provide a reference related to the development of TEV implementation research for high-voltage equipment. From the review conducted, it can be known that there are some common methods for comparing TEV sensor performance with other sensors based on the comparison of PD measurement which is implemented in 6 types of high-voltage equipment. By comparing parameters such as frequency value, occurrence time, duration, PD pattern, waveform shape, etc., a more in-depth analysis of the characteristics of partial discharge detected by TEV or its comparative sensor for each equipment or type of defect can be determined.

articleTitle: Characteristic of Cup-and-Pin Insulator Flashover Voltage under Fan-Shaped Contamination with Various Types and Levels of Pollutant
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Outdoor insulators can be contaminated in a variety of ways. One of them is fan-shaped non-uniform pollution distribution. This type has a point of view that the wind comes continuously from one direction, resulting in a windward side which represents the direction of the incoming flow and a leeward side where the more severe pollutant layer is on a small area of insulator. Not many contaminant parameters have been discussed related to fan-shaped pollution distribution type. This study was to investigate the flashover voltage characteristics of a fan-shaped contaminated insulator by considering the type and level of pollutants. The porcelain cup-and-pin insulators were polluted by various contamination techniques. The flashover testing was conducted after the naturally dried contaminated insulator was subjected to humidity for a certain duration. After the flashover voltages were obtained 10 times, the insulator was measured for the equivalent salt deposit density (ESDD) and non-soluble material deposit density (NSDD) values. The results showed that the proposed contamination technique was quite effective in controlling the level of insulator pollution. The flashover voltage of cup-and-pin insulator with fan-shaped pollution distribution was not only affected by the pollutant weight, but also by the pollutant type.

articleTitle: Negative Corona Discharge from Needle—Plane Electrode: Experiment And Simulation Studies
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In electrical equipment, stressed parts with sharp shapes tend to experience corona discharge more quickly. There are two types of corona discharge: positive and negative. A negative corona discharge is generally characterized by highfrequency and trichel pulses. In this study, the characteristics of negative corona discharges were investigated. The effects of voltage on the peak value, average value, and frequency of the Trichel pulses were analyzed. These three parameters were used as the Trichel pulse parameters. The electrode used was a needle plate. A finite element method (FEM)-based simulation was performed. The measurement and simulation results were compared. The results of the analysis showed that the higher the applied voltage, the higher the value of the Trichel pulse parameters. In the simulation results, the peak current values at the voltage level of −4.25 kV and −4.5 kV are 0.102 mA and 0.106 mA, respectively. The peak current values at the voltage level of −4.25 kV and −4.5 kV on the measurement results are 0.088 mA and 0.092 mA, respectively. The root mean square (RMS) error between the measurement and simulation results was 0.0118. This indicates that the comparison between the experimental and simulation results is on agreement.

articleTitle: Synergistic Effect of Polarity Reversals and Load Current on Life of HVDC Cable Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The paper presents a mathematical model for estimating the degradation/aging of a HVDC cable considering the combined effect of polarity reversal of applied voltage and load current. The load cycle and the polarity reversal cycle are imposed on a 320 kV XLPE insulated DC cable. Electric field and thermal distribution across the XLPE insulation have been obtained using Finite Element Method (FEM). Electric field distribution associated with DC applied voltage on a HVDC cable has been shown and resistive field distribution is reported. A significant rise in electric field across the cable insulation is observed after polarity reversal apparently one of the causes for cable damages. Investigations based on electric field and thermal distribution have been carried out using a standard life estimation model based on Inverse Power Model (IPM) and lifetime of cable insulation has been computed. However, it is observed that lifetime of cable insulation varies significantly across several points of study used for the analysis. The ageing parameter does not represent the predictable trend due to field distribution associated with polarity reversal and temperature distribution associated with load cycle.

articleTitle: Case Study of Internal Partial Discharge in Medium Voltage Power Cable Failure at Rangkasbitung Baru 150kV Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
