abstract: Medium voltage power cable is an equipment to connect power transformer to cubicle feeder. This cable installed in canal or basement. Partial discharge (PD) can determine dielectric condition of power cable in online condition. Partial discharge signal that travels in grounding strap of power cable can be detected and measured by HFCT sensor (High Frequency Current Transformer). Parameters for determining partial discharge source from cable are based on magnitude, PRPD pattern (phase resolve partial discharge) with two cluster, and unipolar waveform. The problem in detecting internal partial discharge is locating the source. Internal partial discharge has spread characteristic. The presence of a single set of cable creates a scenario in which a fault in one of the cables may propagate and affect the remaining wires in the set and will be detected by HFCT. The unique characteristic of internal partial discharge is from unipolar waveform. When unipolar waveform detected, user may check whether power cable have partial discharge source confirmed by magnitude and PRPD analysis support. the case study of power cable failure at Rangkasbitung Baru substation will be shown in this paper when overvoltage occurs from feeder side, one of power cable damage. For making sure other cable ready to operate after disturbance, medium voltage AC (MV AC) test applied to power cable remaining. Some power cable makes hissing sound and then out of operation. Transformer operated with remaining power cable. Partial discharge test applied after transformer re-energized and some power cable has unipolar waveform confirmed with magnitude and PRPD support. The hypothesis is, the cable core might also be damaged due to overvoltage occurred and MV AC tested. Investigation from broken power cable shown cable core is damage and make a treeing pattern across insulation until outer shield going to ground.

articleTitle: Ultimate VHF Broadband Interferometer for Lightning Channel Imager in 3D
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This report is a summary of the VHF Broadband Lightning Channel Imager (VHF LCI), which has been developed over approximately 30 years by the Lightning Research Group of Osaka University’s Graduate School of Engineering (LRGOU). However, its origins can be traced back to the author’s doctoral research in electromagnetic field theory at the Department of Communications Engineering, Osaka University, in the 1970s. Thus, it can be said to span nearly half a century. In the spring of 1979, I took a position as an assistant at the Space-Electronics Research Institute of Nagoya University (Toyokawa, Aichi Prefecture). The first project I became involved in was the measurement of lightning return stroke velocities. This involved arranging multiple photodetectors in parallel and receiving the emitted light signals associated with lightning return strokes from multiple altitudes, with the aim of estimating their velocities based on the time differences. At the time I began this research, Jordan and Uman from the University of Florida had published in the Journal of Geophysical Research (JGR), to the best of my recollection, an article in which they digitized analog signals from streak camera films capturing lightning discharges from different altitudes. However, upon examining their findings, I noticed that the optical signals, which were expected to be proportional to the current pulses, were undergoing deformation as they propagated. This strongly reminded me of the concept of “propagation of electromagnetic pulses in dispersive media” that I had learned in electromagnetic field theory. Suddenly, I became determined to develop a broadband interferometer for the purpose of visualizing lightning discharge channels, based on the concept of electromagnetic pulse propagation. In this presentation, I will look back on the history of the development of the broadband interferometer and also introduce some new insights.

Author Keywords: propagation of electromagnetic pulses in dispersive media

articleTitle: Optimizing the Slot-Pole Combination of a 500 W Brushless DC Motor for Urban Electric Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In designing an electric motor, many parameters come into play that will determine the characteristics and performance of the given motor, for example choosing the slot-pole combination of the motor design. One challenge that also became prevalent on designing an electric motor, especially on an e-bike is geometry limitation which often limited by the rim size. This research propose a method to find the most compatible slot-pole combination of a 500 W brushless DC motor suited for e-bike application. Initial design parameter of the motor that will be used as reference and further developed were based on a 500 W brushless DC motor found on an e-bike conversion kit. Performance requirement of an e-bike were estimated for a given speed and terrain. Several slot-pole combination options were proposed to satisfy those performance requirement. It was then modeled and tested by simulation to see its respective characteristic and performance. From the results, it was concluded that 36-34 slot-pole combination were found to be the most suitable one for the given performance requirement and design parameter constraint. Further validation of the slot-pole combination is performed by variably changed the mechanical load as to represent various terrain condition like flat and uphill road using simulation method as well. On this regard, the proposed design managed to deliver the required torque according to simulated terrain. FEA of the proposed design were also performed and shows good result.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Moving Average to Reduce the Photovoltaic System Active Power Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) system works connected to the electricity network, there is a problem of output power fluctuations. The output power of the PV system fluctuates causing system frequency instability. One way to overcome this problem is to use an energy storage system or an electric spring. The electric spring is a system that reduces the ramp rate or changes in the output power of the PV system suddenly, so that the power system perceives the power it produces changes slowly. This paper proposes a simulation of an electric spring using the moving average method to mitigate fluctuations in the output power of a PV system. The moving average (MA) method intends to average a number of PV system active power output data with an adjustable data size range. The active power output value of an average yield PV system is expected to change slowly or have a low ramp rate. The amount of input and output data becomes wider. Changes in the value of the window length adjust the desire and affect the active power output of the PV system that has been refined. The actual output active power of the PV system at that time will most likely not be equal to its average rated power. The energy storage system uses a type of valve regulated lead acid (VRLA) battery. The selection of batteries takes into consideration from the development, research and commercialization side, if all of these stages have been passed, the energy storage can be said to be mature.

articleTitle: Frequency Analysis on Pulse Train of Lightning Discharge Observed in Malacca, Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Pulse train of lightning discharge is an intracloud event that remains poorly understood especially in Malaysia. Therefore, this paper presents the frequency analysis on pulse train observed in Malacca, Malaysia. This study employed 100 pulse train samples preceding negative subsequent return stroke to be analyzed through wavelet analysis in order to investigate their power spectrum characteristics. All the samples were superimposed with the dart leader of subsequent return stroke. In this regard, the wavelet analysis was employed in this study to investigate the range of power produced by pulse train and the frequency regions of their occurrences. The scalogram of the pulse train signal was produced by using the Mexican Hat wavelet function in Matlab. The spectral and spread frequency regions were measured from the scalogram. In this study, the pulse train samples radiate energy at a range of 7.7 kHz to 403.2 kHz. As for the maximum peak power, the average pulse train generated was 184.6 (V/m)² and can reach up to 2170 (V/m)². These findings enhanced the understanding of lightning physics, particularly on the pulse train characteristics of lightning in Malaysia.

articleTitle: System Identification of a Roller Rig with Factory Default PMSM Drives for Speed Controller Tuning in Speed Synchronized Tractions of an Electric Train Simulator
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper presents a system identification of a roller rig those functions as an electric train traction system simulator. The roller rig is hardware in the loop (HIL) comprising the Matlab Simulink environment, dSPACE ControlDesk (universal experiment software for ECU development), permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driver, and a roller representing the train body. The driver already contains a torque controller with a default setting from the ordinary equipment manufacturer (OEM). This paper identified the dynamics of the roller rig, including the factory default current controller. System identification through experiments revealed that a third-order transfer function could represent its dynamics. Based on this transfer function, the rig speed controller was re-tuned. The experimental results showed that the performance with the re-tuned speed controller is better than the original one.

articleTitle: MACTAM- Mobile And Compact High Voltage Test And Measurement Facility For Educational Purposes
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper presents a mobile and compact High Voltage Test and Measurement facility (macTaM) which enables teaching personal at higher education institutions to realize a powerful practical education in the field of high voltage engineering without the need of a cost and resource consuming high voltage laboratory. It mainly consists out of a shielded compartment with a ground noise level < 1 pC. The front end is based on a control system with an IoT-interface and a standard regulating transformer. By integrating upcycled voltage transformers from medium voltage grids as voltage sources, test voltages up to 25 kV can be reached where the variation of voltage waveform is realized through additional circuitry consisting out of standardized circuit components. The whole facility is designed to meet safety requirements following Safety Integrity Level 3 (SIL 3). The realized setup can be used for a huge variety of laboratory activities in the field of high voltage education. Due to the IoT-interface, practical internet remote teaching is possible when certain IT-equipment is added. The mobile and compact design enables teaching at minimum room requirements and at changing locations.

articleTitle: Comparison of Fault Location Analysis Techniques Used on Sumatra Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Maintaining customer power supply availability is a crucial performance metric for electrical engineers. Customers of electricity distribution companies want a high level of dependability and prompt power restoration when outages occur. With this expectation from the consumer, engineers can speed up power restoration times by identifying defects as accurately as possible. There are numerous ways to find faults in transmission bays. Therefore, it takes a variety of techniques to pinpoint them with the least number of mistakes and at the lowest possible cost. The authors will compile disturbances records on a transmission line in Sumatera Island and determine the best methods for fault detection and how we can develop it. We will utilize the Distance and Line Differential record to import the current and voltage of each disturbance. The authors will attempt to use Simple Reactance, Takagi Method, Double-Ended Impedance, and Travelling Waves to see the fault locator’s features for various fault characteristics in real time data. The user is expected to receive the best approach for identifying disturbances in high-voltage transmission networks with various topologies and types of faults as the final product. Additionally, it is intended that users will be able to access the best technique for determining fault distances in regions like Indonesia that experience many transmission disturbances with high resistance.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Flow and Spray Pattern Characteristics of Biodiesel in a Swirler Burner
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The use of electricity with fuel-fired generators in the form of renewable energy and the use of transportation using electricity and biofuel-based fuels (biofuels) have begun to be encouraged. This study aims to analyze the relationship between fuel and air flow rate to the spray angle of B100 biodiesel, then the initial combustion of B100 biodiesel, and the air velocity flow pattern using a swirler burner. This study can provide hope for environmental sustainability, reduce the greenhouse effect, and ensure the availability of stable raw materials and safety and ease of use. Biodiesel is a renewable fuel derived from vegetable oil with the closest properties to diesel fuel. The biggest challenge to utilizing B100 biodiesel is the value of higher viscosity and density than diesel fuel; this makes biodiesel B100 very difficult to burn. This study is experimentally based using a lab scale industrial swirled type burner by varying the mass flow rate of biodiesel B100 4.50 x 10-3 kg/s, 5.40 x 10-3 kg/s, 6.30 x 10-3 kg/s, 7.20 x 10-3 kg/s, 8.10 x 10-3 kg/s, and 9.00 x 10-3 kg/s. Furthermore, variations in the airflow rate are 0.08 kg/s, 0.12 kg/s, 0.16 kg/s, 0.19 kg/s, and 0.22 kg/s. The results of this study are that with the swirler a vortex flow is formed, which causes biodiesel B100 to burn and can maintain its flame. Then the spray angle decreases for each increase in air mass flow rate, and the initial angle of combustion of B100 biodiesel decreases for each increase in air mass flow rate.

articleTitle: Coal Switching Evaluation on Coal-Fired Power Plants: Case Study in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesia’s energy mix is still dominated by coal, reaching 67.21% in 2022. On the other hand, the coal crisis is a significant challenge to providing electricity needs. Hence, the coal specifications consumed are commonly lower than the coal-fired power plant’s design. In addition, efficiency is essential to reduce production costs, and coal switching is an alternative resolution to keep electricity production. This study compares two coal with a calorific value of 4,500 kcal/kg and 4,200 kcal/kg by considering the equivalent availability factor (EAF), equivalent forced outage rate (EFOR), production cost, and environmental aspect in six months period. The result shows EAF are 89.65% and 89.36%, EFOR 2.98% and 4.02%, cost savings on fuel components is 9.07-32.80 Rp/kWh, and emission concentration is below the standard. It was found that the coal switching program did not have a negative impact on operational, financial, and environmental aspects.

articleTitle: Implementation of Risk Assessment in Determining the Optimal Decision Making with Risk Cost Benefit Output in Transformer Replacement
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Power transformers have an important role in transferring energy from power plants to consumers. There are 325 banks of power transformer had been installed in PLN UITJBB which various ages and manufacturers. To manage the assets, PLN UITJBB implemented an asset management system based on ISO 55001. One of asset management objectives is to fulfill transmission service quality level. However, transformer failures will not fulfill the objective. PLN UITJBB had developed a model to determine the risk of transformer failure. When determining the appropriate mitigation decisions for transformer assets, it is not only based on health index but also on the probability of failure of the asset, which serves as an input in conducting a risk assessment for the transformer. Of course, there is not just one mitigation option due to budget considerations and limited execution time, also known as workability. Therefore, several mitigation options are considered, considering their risks, costs, and benefits before deciding to replace the transformer asset. This paper discusses the implementation of risk assessment in supporting optimal and targeted mitigation decisions for transformer assets at Angke and Teluk Naga substations.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Framework for Automatic Detection of Defective Solar Photovoltaic Cells in Electroluminescence Images Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The utilization of electroluminescence (EL) imaging has proven to be a reliable and precise method for inspecting photovoltaic (PV) modules, due to its high spatial resolution, which allows for the detection of various types of defects. However, the manual analysis of EL images is both expensive, and time-consuming, and requires a specialist with extensive knowledge to identify a wide range of defects. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based technique for the automatic detection of defective solar cells from EL images. Specifically, we employed two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures in our proposed framework. The first architecture is a transfer learning-based VGG16 model that has been fine-tuned with custom fully connected neural network layers to classify defective and non-defective solar cells. The second architecture is a lightweight CNN model that was created from scratch and was used as a baseline for classification comparison with the VGG16 fine-tuned model. The models were trained on a publicly available monocrystalline solar cell image dataset. To address overfitting and to increase the dataset size, we utilized data augmentation techniques. Our proposed method achieved a 95.2% accuracy on the test dataset, which is higher than in previous studies. The implementation of our proposed method will enable continuous, rapid, and precise quality inspection of solar PV plants. Proper maintenance of solar PV panels can significantly improve their efficiency, safety, and power output.

articleTitle: Emerging and Evaluating Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Network for Load Forecast in Java Bali System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019 resulted in a decrease in Java Bali’s total load instead of the usual increasing trend. The loads also exhibit different characteristics in their daily, weekly, and monthly load profiles in each region. The basic statistical coefficient method used to forecast the load introduces a higher possibility of error and inaccuracies in operational planning. A different approach is necessary to achieve higher accuracy in load forecasting. One method to predict reliable trends is deep learning, a subfield of machine learning, which can synthesize the learning curve based on available data. A method called Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM), included in Deep Learning and popularized by researchers since 2000, has shown better accuracy in forecasting. This paper focuses on reviewing the LSTM method for short-term load forecasting in the Java Bali power system using several additional inputs. The method demonstrates an accurate learning curve after the addition of several input parameters.

articleTitle: Ferroresonance in Medium Voltage Transformer: A Review of Failure Investigation, Effect, and Mitigation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Introduction Ferroresonance is a phenomenon that can occur in medium voltage transformers when certain conditions are met. In medium voltage transformers, ferroresonance can occur when the voltage on the primary side of the transformer changes rapidly, and the load on the secondary side is disconnected. This can cause the voltage on the secondary side to rise rapidly, producing high voltages and creating a dangerous situation. In extreme cases, ferroresonance can cause the transformer to explode, leading to catastrophic damage to the surrounding equipment. There are several techniques to mitigate ferroresonance in medium voltage systems, such as: to use a ferroresonance suppressor, which is a passive device that is connected in parallel with the transformer; Install a surge arrester or a metal oxide varistor (MOV) on the secondary side of the transformer to suppress voltage transients; Install a damping circuit to reduce the effect of ferroresonance. This can include a resistor, capacitor, or a combination of the two; Install a fuse on the primary side of the transformer to prevent overvoltage; etc. This paper reviews the results of the investigation resulting from the failure in 20kV/100V medium voltage transformer on the medium voltage side of the incoming transformer unit 3 at Pantai Indah Kapuk substation which is suspected to be due to ferroresonance along with the resulting impacts and mitigation recommendations.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Circular Patch Microstrip Antenna (CPMA) for Detecting Partial Discharge on High Voltage Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) is a phenomenon that occurs at high voltage. PD measurement are crucial for determining the insulation condition of high-voltage equipment. One of the methods used to detect PD is the UHF method, which involves installing an antenna sensor. This paper presents a gradual parameter optimization approach for the circular microstrip patch antenna (CPMA) by adjusting the parameter values from the reference design. The proposed parameters such as feedline width (A), groundplane length (G), resistive loading width (F), and arm length (B). The optimization is performed gradually on these four parameters (A, G, F, and B). The objective of this optimization is to enhance the antenna’s performance and maximize PD detection in high-voltage equipment. In this study, the optimized results achieve a frequency bandwidth of 2.43 GHz, which is wider than the bandwidth of the reference design.

articleTitle: Simulation, VNA Test, and Calibration of Improvement Partial Discharge Detector Using Pi-Attenuator Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: A partial discharge is a localized electrical discharge that partially connects conductors’ insulation and could happen near the conductors. IEC-60270 suggests that the direct voltage method can detect partial discharges by utilizing an appropriate impedance circuit, which enhances the transfer of the discharge current when matched to the partial discharge measurement circuit’s impedance. This research simulated and tested circuits using Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) and Partial Discharge (PD) calibrator. The simulation results indicate that the circuit with the most favorable properties has an attenuation value of 1-6 dB. In the experiment section, three detectors were tested, detector A with an attenuation of 3dB, detector B with an attenuation of 4dB, and detector C with an attenuation of 5 dB. The VNA test results show that detector A has a gain of 12dB, the highest among the three detectors. Detector B has a gain of - 13dB, and detector C has a gain of 10dB. An impulse signal with a fixed charge of 100pC, 1nC, and 10nC is given to calibrate the detectors. The calibration results indicate that the voltage measured by each detector differs. Detector A generates the highest voltage, while detector B generates the smallest voltage.

articleTitle: Method To Improve The Accuracy Of PV Curtailment To Maintain The System Stability in North Sulawesi and Gorontalo Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The penetration of renewable energy with high intermittencies, such as solar power, presents a challenge for the North Sulawesi and Gorontalo power grid. Currently, the largest photovoltaic plant in the region is Likupang PV with a capacity of 15 MWp, followed by Isimu PV with a capacity of 10 MWp. The daytime peak load of the electrical system is 330 MW, with the initial penetration of photovoltaics into the system at 7.58%. Due to the low stiffness of the system, which was measured at 22.32 Mw/Hz in 2022, the intermittence has a direct impact on the system’s operation. The study method used for PV curtailment first determines the magnitude by analyzing the correlation between changes in multiple PV and changes in demand affecting frequency. The Pearson correlation coefficient is used to determine the magnitude of the correlation among these variables. If Likupang PV has a significant influence on changes in frequency, then it can become a curtailment target to limit the amount of power change due to intermittence. Secondly, through data mining, we can understand the function of the influence of changes in PV power on frequency changes. From this function, we can determine the operating limits of the PV to achieve the desired frequency operating range. Thirdly, in this study, this function is tested through simulations and experiments in the field to verify the accuracy of the required PV curtailment execution. By applying this approach, business owners can optimize the planning, regulation, and reliability of the electricity system, thereby mitigating power interruptions in solar power plants.

articleTitle: Effect of Conductor Notches Size Inside of 150kV Gas Insulated Switchgear Spacer on Electric Field Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper discusses novel method to significantly reduce electric field stress on gas insulated switchgear (GIS) spacer mainly at its triple junction area. Spacer is secondary insulation used in GIS, with it primary insulation being gas. Spacer is used to hold conductor inside GIS so that it doesn’t move and remain stationary during its operational. Spacer has been well known as most vulnerable part of GIS Installation, and its vulnerability could be traced back at triple junction area. This area is where SF6 gas, Spacer, and Conductor meet, and due to its high electric field nature, is one of the causes of Spacer failure. To further increase its mechanical strength property, notches is added inside spacer to hold conductor bulge to fill said notches). This paper tests the effect of said notches on electric field distribution both inside and on the surface (mainly at its triple junction area). Size of notches is varied from 6mm to 24mm with 3mm increment. The result suggests that that the smaller the conductor notches, the intensity of electric field will increase. It is also observed that, the change of conductor notches size inside spacer will have effect on spacer surface. Increasing the size of conductor notches inside spacer could potentially reduced electric field intensity on triple junction area by more than 80% compared to original design with 3mm notches.

articleTitle: Business Scheme for EV Charging Station & Impact Load Penetration On Distribution Network System of Airport : Case Study International Airport Soekarno-Hatta, Tangerang Banten
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: To increase the population of electric vehicles and charging stations, the Indonesian government has planned acceleration programs related to electric vehicles and facilities. Use electric vehicles as well as alternative solutions for transportation for realizing energy clean, quality air clean, lower gas emissions, and a friendly environment. This thing expected could guard endurance energy with a reduction fuel oil consumption. In line with the government program, PT Angkasa Pura II currently it’s also being to do acceleration of implementing electric vehicle charging stations in International Airport Soekarno Hatta – Tangerang Banten Indonesia, with creating a roadmap charging station for electric vehicles from 2023-2030. Based on data references and the use of the Monte Carlo method for forecasting the number of electric vehicles that will enter the airport area, the estimated number of public electric vehicle charging stations will be installed from 2023-2030. This paper will be an analysis of pricing and business scheme for electric vehicle charging stations in the airport area and study the impact charging stations load on the electrical distribution system in International Airport Soekarno Hatta – Tangerang Banten Indonesia for additional electrical loads from electric vehicle charging stations.

articleTitle: Linear Programming Approach Based Demand Response to Support Intermittent and Non-Disptachable Renewable Energies Penetration in Nusa Penida Iconic Island
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: During the energy transition, the electricity supply in the isolated island should change from fossil fuel to renewable energy. Since the renewable energy sources on the island are limited and have unique characteristics as intermittent and non-dispatchable sources, the operation of the grid should be modified. One of the solutions for reliability supply during the operation of intermittent and non-dispatchable energy resources is demand response. In the model, the demand response uses Demand Response Programs (DRP) with the Linear Programming Approach (LP) method. In the case study, the implementation of the DRP Linear programming method can increase system reliability, minimize the total operating costs of power plants, and benefit electricity consumers and electricity supply business plans (PLN) by reducing load demand in specific periods, especially during minimum availability of the intermittent and non-dispatchable resources.

articleTitle: Study of EMI Shielding Performance of CNT-filled Epoxy Resin
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: With the increased demand for multifunctional carbon-based composite materials in the aeronautical industry, there is a need for developing advanced nanostructured composites with superior electrical and mechanical properties. Carbon nanotubes (CNT) are a viable filler ingredient for polymer-based nanocomposites because of their high aspect ratio and outstanding electrical conductivity. Electrical conductivity is a major factor in the feasibility of CNT-polymer-based nanocomposite for electromagnetic shielding. A material’s ability to effectively block an electromagnetic field is measured by its shielding effectiveness (SE). The electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness (EMI-SE) of CNT-epoxy nanocomposite in X-band (8–12 GHz) frequency is investigated experimentally in this work. The electrical conductivity of the nanocomposite is measured. The study is performed with different filler loading varying from 0.05 wt% to 3 wt%.

articleTitle: Optimization Design to Increase Efficiency of 350 W Outer Rotor Brushless DC Motor for Urban Electric Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Electric bicycle utilizes an electric motor, such as a brushless DC (BLDC) motor as the main propulsion system. The design criteria for an electric bicycle with a BLDC motor for electric bicycle are determined by the type of bicycle, the track the rider will take, the regulation speed with a maximum speed of 25 km/hour, and the rider’s physique. The challenge in designing an electric motor, especially on an e-bike is geometry limitation which often limited by the maximum frame and tire size. This research is focused on efficiency improvement in BLDC motors for electric bicycles. Efficiency depends on losses, including iron and copper losses. Reduction of the losses generated by the motor leads to better efficiency. In this research, reference BLDC motor is BLDC hub motor in the market with rated power of 350 Watts (W) and 36 slot-40 pole configurations. A reverse-engineering process is carried out to obtain a more optimal design. The analysis is carried out by varying the winding motor parameters such as conductor diameter and the number of strands. In addition, slot and pole variations are also investigated due to relation with the iron loss of the motor. The efficiency more than 80% was achieved with wider diameter and more strand conductor. The 18-20 slot-pole combination were found to be the most suitable for the given performance. With further winding modification, efficiency is increased from 80,98% (reference model) to 84,8 % (proposed model) at 221 rpm and decrease power input from 338 W to 328 W.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Risk Mitigation Against Intentional Attacks for Non-Wire Transmission Expansion Planning Based on Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Currently, transmission expansion planning takes not exclusively the N-l criterion into consideration, but also the grid’s vulnerability risk and newer technologies. Because of its wide expanse and capacity limitations, the extensive transmission network is vulnerable to physical intentional attacks. In addition, transmission expansion planning (TEP) includes renewable energy (RE) technologies as a non-wire expansion option, and its integration enhance system reliability. Using game theory with power flows and probabilistic risk analysis, the problem of the attacker model and defender mitigation of intentional transmission attack risk is addressed. This paper presents a novel method for optimizing the placement and size of renewable energy sources (photovoltaic and batteries), which has been implemented on the IEEE 14-bus test system. In case 1 (photovoltaic without batteries investment), the defender is capable of reducing the vulnerability risk from 112.3 MW to 5S.5MW. In case 2 (photovoltaic with batteries investment), the defender can reduce the risk of vulnerability from 112.3 MW to 70.67 MW. The equilibrium of the attacker-defender game is the defender’s photovoltaic investment of 203.82 MUSD. Further research will consider implementation on larger test case systems or actual power grids.

articleTitle: Assessment of Voltage and E-Field Distribution in Outdoor Composite Insulator in 500 kV System for Interface Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation-based investigation using the finite element method (FEM) for a 500 kV composite insulator with conducting defect generating from the live end. The core of these insulators is Fiber Reinforced Plastic (FRP) glass which has silicone rubber as polymeric housing material around it and metal end fittings. The macroscopic interface between the core rod and polymeric housing is a weak contact and hence prone to degradation in these composite insulators. The appearance of voids at the interface could be due to improper adhesion during manufacturing. Moreover, poor handling during installation can lead to the development of internal cracks leading to permanent damage like brittle fracture. In service, the interfacial condition deteriorates due to internal defects, air-filled voids, and mechanical damage by dynamic loads (aeolian), leading to the debonding or crack at the interface. Hence, detecting internal defects at the early stages is essential for safe, reliable operation and improved service life. Engineering approaches must be employed to assess the performance of the interface to keep the insulator healthy. The field stress has been computed and improved by using a series combination of 132 kV conventional insulators to restrict the propagation of interfacial tracks. Results show a reduction in the stress at the simulated conducting channel, leading to a reduction in the electric field stress, which will restrict the propagation and improve service life.

articleTitle: Power Quality Assessment on Priority Industrial Customers of Java-Bali Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Based on data managed by the Priority Account Executive (PAE) of the Indonesian state electric utility, PLN Head Office, there were 55 of the 238 priority industrial customers have complaints of voltage dips that interfere with the business production process. These customers’ complaints indicated that there was a problem with the quality of the power supplied by PLN. Improving the quality of electric power will be able to increase customer engagement with increasing customer satisfaction. However, currently, there is no firm comprehensive power quality assessment procedure, so it is necessary to study power quality problems for all significant industrial customers in Java-Bali grid to determine the level of power quality, including mapping of power quality data records, customer complaints, and mitigation. Power quality problems analyzed in this study include transient, under-voltage, voltage sag, over voltage, voltage swell, and interruption. Based on the 438 incidents of power quality problems that have the potential to cause disturbances during one year of recorded data, the number of customer complaints obtained from PAE data is only 57 complaints. From the analysis results, 84.2% of customer complaints correspond to the incidence of power quality problems, while 15.8% of customer complaints do not correspond to the incidence of power quality problems. Furthermore, further research needs to be done to improve the power quality service provided by PLN to 84.2% of these customer complaints, while 15.8% of customer complaints that do not correspond to the incidence of power quality problems need to be socialized to customers that the complaints are caused by customers’ equipment. A deep investigation has been done on some industrial customers to find the root cause of the power quality problem and propose mitigation actions to solve the problem.

articleTitle: Estimation of Image Charge on Electrodes in Space Charge Measurements with Pulsed Electroacoustic Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Data from space charge measurements using the Pulsed Electro Acoustic (PEA) system are distorted due to the presence of image charges on the electrodes. The distortion of the signal is significant in the vicinity of the electrodes since injected charge often tends to accumulate in this region. In layered dielectrics, the amount of image charges may be significantly higher due to interfacial charge accumulation. In this paper, equations for image charge estimation in homogeneous and layered dielectrics are formulated. These equations are further applied to space charge data for a 2 layered dielectric sample.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Analysis of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems for Off-grid Small Systems in Remote Areas of Indonesia: A Case Study in Three Locations
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Indonesian government has set forth a plan to enhance the adoption of renewable energy sources (RES) in order to replace diesel generators in numerous off-grid small systems situated in remote areas of Indonesia. The primary objectives of this program in the electricity supply sector are to decrease reliance on fossil fuels, lower production costs, and mitigate environmental emissions. Two RES technologies with significant potential for utilization are PV Photovoltaic and Wind Turbines. During the planning phase, it is crucial to conduct a comprehensive techno-economic study to determine the optimal size and configuration of a Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES). This paper focuses on the analysis of three different locations, each possessing distinct RES potential, which may impact the optimal solution. The study employs Homer as the analytical tool to carry out the analysis.

articleTitle: Hybrid Modeling and Control of Modified Cuk Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: A power converter with switching mode, which is widely used in power electronics circuits, has some advantages including high efficiency, flexible output voltage, and lightweight. One of the power converters with switching mode is the Cuk converter, which can produce an output voltage lower or higher than the input voltage but with reverse voltage polarization. In addition, the Cuk converter also has a capacitor as an isolation between the input and the output side. In previous studies, the Cuk converter was modified so that it has an output voltage polarization that is not reversed like a conventional Cuk converter but with continuous input and output currents like a conventional Cuk converter. Circuits with switching in power electronics will produce hybrid behavior naturally. Control is needed on this switching so that the hybrid behavior of the converter does not cause problems and can overcome disturbances or changes that occur. Modified Cuk converter has a non-linear nature caused by switching activity so non-linear control is needed. The non-linear control design that is generally used for the power converter is complicated. So in this study, the authors proposed a control scheme for a modified Cuk converter based on a hybrid model. The proposed control scheme has the advantage of a simpler and easier design and tuning process. The expected result of this research is a control scheme that is simple and easy to design on this modified Cuk converter which can overcome disturbances or changes that occur in the circuit by giving control commands to the switching.

articleTitle: optimization of Configuration Hybrid Power Generation System at Oil Refinery
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The oil refinery industry has a potential emission reduction by combining its fossil fuel with Renewable Energy usage. One alternative to reduce carbon emissions is the hybrid power system using solar panels for electricity generation. This research will observe the optimum scenario for utilizing a hybrid power system. The research subject is observed refinery facilities that will be built in Indonesia, where the electricity source used formerly comes from fossils. The monitored parameters are Cost of Energy (COE) and carbon emission. optimization involves three scenarios involving basic and hybrid configurations. The basic scenario is the initial configuration of the electricity supply with power source from the generator and PLN (national’s utility). The first scenario is a hybrid power plant utilizing the roofs of existing buildings in the refinery area. The second is a hybrid power plant with a battery to supply electricity at night, at the capacity of renewable energy (RE) of 20% and 40%. Compared to the basic scenario, scenario 1 increases COE by 0.17% and reduces carbon emission at 0.3% compared to the basic scenario. Scenario 2 with 20% and 40% of renewable energy are obtained at COE of 4.7% and 44.3%, while reducing emissions occurred at 38% and 52.7%, respectively. The scenario of a hybrid power system with a 20% renewable energy is the optimal result compared to the other scenarios.

articleTitle: 20kV Busbar Protection Design Development to Overcome Various Disturbances Caused by Transformer Loading Configurations
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In 2019, PLN UIT JBB (Western Java Transmission Main Unit) implemented 20kV busbar protection by coordinating incoming and non-cascade feeder protection. However, when the fault occurs in parallel feeders or when the Feeder is transferred to another busbar transformer with coupler facilities. The 20kV busbar protection design does not work correctly in isolating the faults due to fault coordination logic between busbar protection feeders and incoming. Therefore, the authors propose a new concept by changing the non-cascade protection scheme setting, which initially used a moment fault current sensor of 230% of the Transformer’s nominal current (4000A) to a current sensor from a Time Multiple Setting with a current magnitude of 120% of the nominal current Feeder (320A). The authors also added a 20kV coupler as the 20kV busbar protection part. This scheme has been tested in a laboratory using a multi-tester protection relay with the results. The new design of the 20kV busbar protection can localize the disturbance correctly, being more selective and reliable to accommodate five different types of disturbances.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effectiveness and Efficiency Construction Sea Cable Sumatera - Bangka
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Bangka’s electricity system was currently supplied by Coal-fired Power Plant, Gas-machine power plant, Diesel power plant and Biomass power plant, with a total nett capacity of 197 MW and the highest peak load in 2022 is 180 MW. The peak load growth projection of Bangka Island in 2023 to 2030 is 5.46% per year. Therefore an additional supply of electrical energy is needed to fulfill the supply of electrical energy. PLN Bangka Belitung must implement one of two alternatives to fulfill this condition, there are 2 possible alternatives which are built transmission interconnection to evacuate surplus energy in the Sumatera system or build a new power plant on Bangka Island. Both alternatives will be compared by technical and economic study. This technical study uses power system simulation simulations with an expected output of the transmission loading, voltage and losses between two alternatives. The economic study will compare the present value of total cost between transmission interconnection from the Sumatera system and build a coal-fired power plant in Bangka Island. After analysis, it was found that the transmission interconnection alternatives are the best solution than build coal-fired power plant in Bangka Island.

articleTitle: Assessment of Power Transformer Solid Insulation Condition Using a Composite Index: A Case Study of UIT-JBM Population
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Power transformers are critical component of electric power systems and are expensive assets. The insulation system of power transformers is an essential factor in determining their lifespan. Aging of the transformer paper insulation is an irreversible process, and it is considered as the end-of-life criteria. In recent years, CIGRE TB 761 has published guidelines for transformer paper insulation assessment using multiple parameters to calculate a single index. This study aims to implement the CIGRE TB 761 method on power transformers under the UIT-JBM population. This will allow comparison of solid insulation indices from 357 power transformers. The paper discusses the methodology and presents the results of the assessment of the transformer paper insulation. The study then analyses the correlation between each testing parameters and combined paper insulation index with transformer operating age.

articleTitle: SWOT Analysis of Utilization of Nuclear Power Plants to Support Net Zero Emissions in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The electricity and heat sectors produce enormous CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions as a greenhouse gas which destroys the ozone layer. Many CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions come from burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas in power generation. Coal Fired Power Plants (CFPP) supply more than 50% of electricity in Indonesia. The Indonesian government plans a zero-carbon program in 2060 where the Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) starts operating in 2045. This study aims to analyze the use of NPP in the program. Strength weakness opportunity and threat (SWOT) analysis is used to examine the utilization of NPP from a technical, economic, and social perspective. From the analysis and discussions, it is concluded that NPP has strengths, namely low CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission, high operational reliability, and has a large economic impact. The weaknesses of the NPP include the relatively high LCOE, high overnight costs, fuel supply risk, and public concern about safety. NPP opportunities in Indonesia are sustainable economic growth and electricity, the CFPP early retirement program, and public opinion that supports NPP development. While the NPP threats are the high potential for earthquakes and tsunamis in Indonesia which can trigger NPP accidents, a significant reduction in the cost of renewable energy, especially PV modules, and political issues.

articleTitle: Improving Power Quality in Double-Stage Single-Phase Grid-Conneted PV Inverter System using MPPT-FLC-PSO and FLCs
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper presents a double-stage control for a single-phase grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) converter-inverter system using fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs). The converter stage utilizes a maximum power point tracking (MPPT)-based FLC with a voltage-based search space reduction strategy is used to enhance tracking control response. Two additional FLCs are incorporated in the inverter stage to simultaneously regulate the DC-linked voltage for power flow balancing and control the grid current for improved power quality. Through particle swarm optimization (PSO), the topology and fuzzy parameters of the FLCs are optimized, thereby eliminating conventional design, and reducing computational complexity. The proposed PSOFLCs are implemented and evaluated on a 2.5 kW PV system. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed FLCs in increasing energy utilization efficiency and inverter efficiency up to 10% compared to classical and conventional controllers, including reduce total harmonic distortions of grid-current and achieve near-unity power factor.

articleTitle: Improving The Reliability of MV Busbar Protection by IEC61850 GOOSE Message: A Case Study in PT PLN (Persero) 150 kV New Jatake Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The IEC 61850 standard is an international standard for automation and communication systems at substations, which introduces Ethernet-based communication for exchanging information between protection and control devices at substations. In addition, IEC 61850 also defines server-to-server communication called the generic objectoriented substation event (GOOSE) Message as a fast message transmission service. When implemented in the protection, control, and metering systems of a substation, IEC 61850 GOOSE messages offer numerous benefits, including speed, reduced wiring, and flexibility. On the other hand, it creates new challenges within its application, such as the irrelevance of several commonly used documents, wiring diagrams, and tools. This can happen due to the replacement of hard wired into an ethernet network, resulting in different methods of design, configuring and testing mechanisms when implementing IEC 61850 GOOSE messages. This paper will discuss the application of IEC 61850 GOOSE messages to the New Jatake Substation Transformer protection system. The process of practical design, configuration, and testing will be discussed completely with new documents, diagrams, and tools. Applying IEC 61850 GOOSE Message to transformer protection at substations provides flexibility and speed in its application while maintaining selective and reliable results.

articleTitle: The Projection of Energy Demand of Papua Region to Face the Decentralization and Greenhouse Emission Challenge until 2060
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesia, known for its vast area and expansive oceans, faces significant implications in overall energy planning. Since the political turmoil in 1998, the country has been driving decentralization efforts, necessitating active participation from all provinces in energy management. These roles have gained critical importance due to the mounting pressure of energy transition and the imperative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in line with the commitments made in The Paris Agreement of 2015. Despite these nationwide efforts, Papua Island, a region within Indonesia, has encountered challenges in crafting its province-specific energy planning documents, primarily attributed to limited data availability and a shortage of energy research expertise. The complexity has intensified following the expansion of the province from 2 to 5 regions in 2022. While awaiting streamlined bureaucratic arrangements, the demand projections and energy management from the Papua region remain essential for monitoring and evaluating Indonesia’s overall energy transition towards achieving the Net Zero Emission’s target by 2060. This research calculates the baseline for energy demands, a crucial element in facilitating the energy transition, based on historical data. To project energy demand until 2060, alongside historical data, economic targets, and population projections, various energy intervention policies have been applied. These interventions are categorized into two scenarios: business as usual and sustainable development. Utilizing the Low Emission Analysis Platform (LEAP) for simulation, the study demonstrates that with appropriate energy planning policies, Papua Island can actively contribute to meeting its regional energy demand without compromising the environmental impact in the future. The energy final demand projection in Papua is estimated to be 41,149 thousand barrels of oil equivalent (BOE).

articleTitle: Comparison of the Degree of Polymerization Model of the Transformer and Lifetime
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformer is one of the essential components of electrical power systems. Condition of electrical equipment have been studied to increase system reliability, availability, safety, and to reduce the total cost of assets. In order to extend the service life and to anticipate unintended outages, asset management is needed to assess the condition of equipment. This article aims to provide a comparative review of transformer aging based on degree of polymerization. Insulation deterioration indicates lifetime expectancy of transformers. Oil analysis is one of the diagnoses that can be performed without de-energizing of the transformer. A fault in the transformer can be identified by the production of fault gases. Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is used to identify the condition of transformer based on the gases dissolved in the insulating liquid of transformer. The degree of polymerization (DP) of insulation paper represents the insulation degradation. It can be used as an indication index to measure the insulation age of a transformer. Furan compounds are compounds that are formed when solid insulation is degraded. Furans and the degree of polymerization have a high correlation. A transformer’s lifetime is estimated based on furans compound. The simulation using MATLAB shows that there are disparities between 2-furaldehyde (2FAL) increase and a change in lifetime. The study case shows that the end of lifetime depends on the insulation lifetime based on the concentration of2FAL. It allows time for maintenance planning.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assessment of Small Batch Advanced Metering Infrastructure Utilization on Java Region to Support Indonesian Smart Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) is the breakthrough path to implement the Indonesian smart grid system. The topology of small batch AMI utilization in the Java Region consists of a smart meter, communication media, data concentrator unit, head-end system, and meter data management system. By applying this technology, it can allow a government state-owned electricity company (PLN) to enable a two-way real-time energy monitoring system for supporting smart grid applications. It also has other benefits, such as simplifying the billing collection process and providing realtime event notification to monitor energy meter activities. On Java Regional Business, PLN has implemented AMI in three different locations (Bandung, Jakarta, and Surabaya). The goal of this small batch AMI implementation in Java Regional Business is to provide pre-commercial references and several evaluations for a future large-scale rollout implementation. The evaluation of small batch AMI implementation in Java regional businesses will be discussed, along with a deep dive into the preproduction process, customer installation, and performance evaluation. The end results of this evaluation will allow PLN to have a better view of a forthcoming large-scale project of advanced metering infrastructure to support smart grid system development in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Impact of Power Quality of Microgrids with High Penetration of Renewable Energy on the Characteristics of LED Lamp
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Microgrids are an increasingly popular solution for providing communities and facilities with a reliable, efficient, and resilient energy supply. In a microgrid, several energy sources are combined to form a small self-contained grid that can operate independently of the main grid. Renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydropower are playing an increasingly important role in microgrid design due to their environmental sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and ability to provide a reliable energy supply. However, integrating renewable energy sources into microgrids can pose technical challenges, particularly regarding the electrical equipment within the system. This study aims to explore the effects of power quality on the performance of electrical equipment, specifically LED lamps, within microgrids that feature significant integration of renewable energy sources. Simulation testing will be carried out using the microgrid model in the electric power system simulation software (OPAL-RT) scenario. The output voltage from the microgrid simulation was used to power the LED lamps, and the light emitted by the lamps was analyzed using a spectrophotometer. The results showed that voltage and frequency fluctuations affect the power consumption and efficiency of LED lights in the microgrid, which can affect the overall system performance, stability, and possibly the lifetime. This study provides insight into the challenges and opportunities in integrating renewable energy sources into microgrids and can contribute to sustainable development in the energy sector.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Comparison in Application of Power System Instability Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This research paper aims to compare machine learning techniques for detecting transient instability in power systems. The delayed construction of infrastructure and the increasing presence of converter-based power plants, which reduce system inertia, contribute to operating states that can lead to instability. In such scenarios, disturbances in the network backbone can disrupt system synchronism, potentially causing angle instability and leading to blackouts. Transient stability, characterized by rapid responses before a blackout, requires proactive defense schemes to predict the outcomes of disturbances and take preventive actions. However, predicting whether a disturbance will lead to instability or not is challenging due to multiple factors involved. Machine learning techniques offer the ability to address this challenge by leveraging their capacity for problem generalization. The results shows that several machine learning algorithms have very good accuracy to predict transient instability.

articleTitle: SoC-Temperature Based Power Sharing Algorithm for Battery Racks in Grid Ancillary Services
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The battery pack lifetime is severely affected by the State-of-Charge (SOC) and operating temperature. This paper proposes a real-time SoC-Temperature balance power-sharing algorithm for the battery racks to optimize the battery life. The control scheme takes into account the SoC disparity and temperature deviation simultaneously to calculate the active power set-points for battery energy storage system (BESS) units. The proposed algorithm can serve as an alternative to the state of the health (SoH) based power sharing algorithms, which require complex SoH estimation procedures and extensive data for battery age prediction. This method can be particularly useful for second-life batteries, which often show significant heterogeneity in age, internal resistance, and capacity, necessitating a generic yet robust control strategy for their optimal utilization and to minimize degradation. Simulation results demonstrate (i) the suitability of the proposed control scheme for real-time implementation, (ii) the controller efficacy to limit high battery temperatures, which can help to slow down the ageing process. Overall, this research enables the easy integration of second-life batteries for grid ancillary services, obviating the need for complex SoH estimation procedures by considering battery temperature and SoC.

articleTitle: Methods to Estimate the Likelihood of Failure of Individual Asset in a Power System Business
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: An asset-intensive business’s success relies on the organization’s ability to manage risks. One of the critical risks is related to the in-service asset’s failure. Many organizations use asset health indices (AHI) or scoring and criticality matrices to estimate asset risks. The model selection depends on many factors, including the business requirements, cost and benefit consideration, the criticality of assets, people’s capability, and data availability. This paper provides different methods for estimating the likelihood of asset failure in a power system business consisting of generation, transmission, and distribution assets. The first is the deterministic method by developing an AHI model involving Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA) and Failure Mode Effect and Criticality Analysis (FMECA). The output of AHI is a score representing the likelihood of a failure mode occurring. The second is the statistical lifetime analysis, which involves processing an asset population’s historical failure and survival data. The method assumes that the behavior of the asset population represents the individuals in it. The third is the simplest, i.e., by justifying the asset service time with a reference, such as a manufacturer’s technical lifetime guarantee. The paper also provides examples of implementing each method in a power system case study owned by PLN Indonesia.

articleTitle: Island Stability Improvement Through Defense Scheme and Generation Control Parameters Optimization: Case Study in Central Kalimantan System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Kalimantan Interconnection System encompasses an extensive transmission network spanning approximately 5985 kilometers, with radial lines constituting nearly 60% of the entire system. Steam power plants contribute significantly to the system’s power generation, accounting for approximately 70% of the total capacity. However, these power plants exhibit limited responsiveness to demand fluctuations. In 2022, the system experienced 395 transmission disruptions, of which 315 were successfully restored, while 80 resulted in permanent trips, resulting in a total downtime of 5692 minutes. The Central Kalimantan system operates using a radial topology and includes a 200 MW power plant located at the end of the line, referred to as the SLK steam power plant. Despite its potential for island operation, the Central Kalimantan system encounters operational challenges such as challenging terrain, load-generation imbalances, high-voltage phenomena, and oscillation phenomena. Successful island operation relies heavily on optimizing defense schemes and parameter control from the power plant. If operational parameters like voltage, power flow, and current experience extreme oscillations that cannot be balanced by the power plant, blackouts can occur, leading to adverse effects on the company and the power plant operator. This paper proposes a strategy to enhance the success of island operations by combining defense scheme optimization and parameter control from the power plant. The Central Kalimantan system employs various defense schemes, including over-voltage transmission shedding, under-frequency load shedding, and an adaptive defense scheme. Additionally, the power plant is optimized through Island Mode Operation (IMO) including overspeed protection control, power system stabilizer tuning, dashboard monitoring island, and houseload operation. Based on disruption statistics from 2020 to February 2023, 20% of incidents occurred before island operation optimization, while 80% occurred after optimization. The success rate of island operation reaches 100% when optimization is conducted, whereas it drops to 0% in the absence of optimization.

articleTitle: Co-firing of Coconut Frond with Coal Blends in Coal-Fired Power Plant: Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Co-firing testing with a 5% coconut frond was carried out at a power plant with a capacity of 25 MWe to determine changes in the main parameters of the power plant, production costs, and the environment. Mixing coal fuel with coconut frond biomass is carried out in the coal yard. The biomass of coconut fronds has a higher content of ash, total moisture, and volatile matter than coal. In the meantime, the sulfur content and calorie value are lower by 2,308 kcal/kg as-Received base (Ar) compared to 3,990 kcal/kg of coal (Ar). Mixed fuels have the potential corrosion induction of chlorine of the minor category and the potential for slagging and fouling low and medium categories. The average temperature of the bed furnace area tends to drop but is still within the operating limit range (less than 950 °C). The temperature in the upper furnace area and Furnace Exit Gas Temperature (FEGT) when co-firing has increased and has already exceeded the standard limit with a range of 948 °C to 976°C. Total water flow increased by 1.87 t/h. The total mass flow of flue gas increased by 3%. The absorption of heat energy in the superheater area and water spray increased by 5.30% and 4.31%, respectively. Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) also increased by 0.97%. Economically, co-firing 5% coconut frond releases saves fuel costs of 0.16 Rp/kWh. The average SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions increased slightly, but the average NOx emissions dropped from 330.4 mg/Nm3 to 290.5 mg/Nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It is necessary to pay attention to mixing coal fuel with biomass to ensure homogeneity. This study only evaluates the impact of short-term changes on the power plant, so additional research is required to evaluate the medium-and long-term effects.

articleTitle: Determination of Optimal Number of Spare Transformer Using Probabilistic Method: A Study Case of Pematangsiantar Distribution Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Transformer failure is an event that is difficult to avoid, especially in distribution networks where thousands of distribution transformers must be maintained for reliability. A Transformer is an important piece of equipment in the distribution of electricity to customers where one distribution substation has only one transformer. The case study of the Pematangsiantar Distribution Unit has more than five thousand transformers (20kV/400V) to serve low voltage customers, namely 0.45 kVA - 197 kVA power. The transformer capacity which is the object of research is 25 kVA-250 kVA. Determination of the optimal number of spare transformers is carried out using the Poisson Distribution probability method by comparing the desired level of reliability, the Mean Time Between failures (MTBF), and Statistical Economics. The result of the case is the most number of spare transformers is MTBF, Reliability, and Statistical Economic criterion respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Various Transformer Field Conditions Using Cross-Combined Frequency Response Analysis to Identify Specific Deformity
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: In HV equipment, the most critical and valuable components used is transformers. Power transformers should go through standard diagnostic tests to identify deterioration or to avoid the emergence of defects that might possibly cause severe failure. Frequency Response Analysis already proven to be a promising tool in diagnostic techniques that make use of this understanding to find such changes. FRA has so far been used to detect deformation in transformers by observing changes in the frequency response curve, despite a limited understanding of what caused the changes in the initial case. Several FRA methods have been implemented recently all around the world, primarily for transformer deformation detection and diagnosis. Nonetheless, there is now an increasing amount of research focused on determining specifically the type and degree of deformation in a transformer by looking at its FRA response curve. It is very important to refer to the guidance given in the recently published IEC, IEEE, SPLN, and CIGRE standards to ensure the accuracy of the analysis of the frequency response results. An approach for transformer diagnostics is discussed in this research by doing a comparative analysis with four study cases related to various physical phenomena and examining the cross-combined between standards and field FRA results. Four FRA measurement cases are taken from the experience in PLN, namely: Tayan (water contamination), Sanggau (transformers relocation), Sambas (rebuilding transformer foundation), and Cianjur (earthquake). The evaluation results indicate that the IEEE and IEC diagnostic standards have an assessment that is closest to the actual condition that is influenced by variations in wide band frequency measurement.

articleTitle: Long Term Projection of Energy Demand in Kalimantan Region: LEAP Model Application
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Energy is a critical element in driving economic sectors, with oil being a significant feedstock worldwide. Its strategic importance is undeniable in supporting the global economy. However, consumerization, which refers to excessive consumption and dependence on resources, has contributed to crises in numerous countries across different regions. Energy consumption is also a severe problem worldwide, especially in industrialized countries, including Kalimantan, Indonesia. The dominant primary energy type in the energy supply mix in 2020 is coal, accounting for about 38.5% of the national total, followed by oil at about 32.8%, gas at about 17.4%, and the rest at about 11.3% through New Renewable Energy (NRE). Therefore, it is necessary to review the energy planning. This paper examines the Long Term Projection of Energy Demand in the Kalimantan Region. Scenarios that are developed include historical data and intervention, which are simulated using the Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) software. In addition, the basic assumptions used to obtain the projections of population to 2045 are derived from PMAS documents but use a flat or sustainable growth rate of 0.3% from 2045 to 2060, while the GDP growth rate is calculated as a critical resource based on Macro Planning Statistical Analysis (PMAS) by BAPPENAS, Indonesia's National Development Planning Agency. The results of this study are essential to determine the electrification energy demand in Indonesia from various sectors such as the household, commercial, industry, transportation, and others sectors. Thus, the result shows that Kalimantan's household sector electrification energy demand recorded a 2.14% growth rate, while the commercial and industrial sectors energy demand recorded higher growth rates of 6.98% and 6.41%, respectively. The transportation sector, the road transportation sector, which is expected to grow significantly in the future, is the most significant contributor to electricity demand. Road transportation sector electrification energy demand recorded a 25.25%.

articleTitle: PMU Optimal Placement Based On N-0 and N-1 Contingency as Preparation of WAMPAC Implementation to Provide Complete System Observability in Khatulistiwa and Interconnection System of Kalimantan
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The development of complex electric power systems necessitates comprehensive monitoring of various parameters, particularly stability parameters such as damping ratio, rotor angle, and oscillation frequency. Traditional SCADA monitoring systems are inadequate due to slow data transmission. Phasor Measurement Units (PMU) have gained attention for their ability to provide high-speed and accurate data on voltage, current magnitudes, and angles for power system monitoring and control. However, PMU procurement and installation are costly, necessitating an optimization process for selecting PMU locations. This paper focuses on optimizing PMU placement using the Binary Integer Linear Programming (BILP) method, considering N-0 and N-1 contingencies. The study is conducted on the Kalimantan system, which comprises the Khatulistiwa System (West Kalimantan) and the Kalimantan Interconnection System (Central, South, and East Kalimantan). Simulation results indicate that the existing system (N-0) requires 7 PMUs for the Khatulistiwa System and 28 PMUs for the Kalimantan Interconnection System. For the N-1 contingency, the numbers increase to 12 units for the Khatulistiwa System and 44 units for the Kalimantan Interconnection System. The PMU requirements until 2025 are also assessed as part of the WAMPAC (Wide Area Monitoring, Protection, and Control) implementation roadmap, based on PT. PLN’s (Persero) RUPTL. Additionally, the WAMPAC topology for the Kalimantan system and the security mechanism for PMU communication are presented to ensure data exchange security.

articleTitle: A Review of Techno-economic Analysis and Size Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems Using Homer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Indonesian government plans to increase the utilization of renewable energy sources (RES) to replace the role of diesel generators in many off-grid small systems in Indonesia’s remote areas. The purposes of the program in the electricity supply business are to reduce dependency on fossil fuels, reduce production costs, and reduce emissions to the environment. The RES generators that have the potential to be used are PV Photovoltaic and Wind Turbines. At the planning stage, a techno-economic study is required to determine the optimal Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) size and configuration. This requires software tools to design, calculate, and optimize the systems. One of the software researchers have widely used is Hybrid optimization Model for Electric Renewables (HOMER) software developed by National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), United States. This paper will review some articles which use Homer for optimal planning of HRES

articleTitle: Investigation of SiO2/ATH/TiO2 Micro-nanofillers to Improve Performance of Silicone Rubber toward UV Radiation and Partial Discharge on High Voltage Outdoor Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: This paper discusses the characteristics of polymer insulator matrix from RTV683 composites with micro-nanofillers to improve the performance of polymer insulators. Research is expected to obtain a new polymer insulator matrix with the best filler composition that is effectively applied to high-voltage outdoor insulators in tropical climates. Investigations were conducted to develop new materials that can improve hydrophobic performance by reducing partial discharge and increasing the UV resistance of silicone rubber insulators.
