The method used was to choose the material with the best performance and then combine it to overcome the obstacles of applying polymer insulators as outdoor high-voltage insulators. Furthermore, developing a manufacturing method for making a polymer insulator matrix using RTV683 silicone rubber with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, ATH, and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> micro-nanofillers. Insulator matrix fabrication using mixers under vacuum conditions for filler dispersion and elimination ofvoids in polymer insulator matrix. Testing and analysis of polymer insulator matrix characteristics including physical, electrical, and chemical tests according to IEC standards include hydrophobic transfer, water diffusion, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), partial discharge (PD), and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The results showed that the RTV683 polymer insulator matrix with a combination of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, ATH, and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> micro-nanofillers has the potential to improve the performance of high-voltage polymer insulators.

articleTitle: Battery Lifetime Prediction Using Cycle Estimation in De-dedieselization Program
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The De-dieselization Program has been launched by PT. PLN (Persero) as one of the expedient approaches towards attaining the goal of a 23% share of renewable energy in the national energy blend in 2025. The project comprises multiple and widely distributed standalone microgrids scattered across remote regions in Indonesia. Typically, the arrangement of the system at each location is small and isolated systems that are not interconnected with the interconnection grid. Each microgrid consists of PV (Photovoltaic) and BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) designed to supply energy to the loads. These facilities are also expected to operate in a hybrid mode with the existing diesel generators. Many microgrid facilities in Indonesia have used BESS as an energy storage technology. The BESS lifespan can be reduced due to the fluctuation in output power of a microgrid caused by renewable energy generation sources such as PV. Frequent replacement of the BESS can substantially increase the operating costs of a project, given that it has a limited lifespan and is the costliest component of a microgrid. The cycle counting method to assess BESS lifespan using properties in PLEXOS has been conducted on LiFePO4, a li-ion battery. According to the conducted study, the accumulation of battery cycles is significantly influenced by the SOC condition and battery capacity. The impact of battery capacity on system parameters, such as unserved energy and generation capacity curtailed, is also demonstrated in this report. It is found that cycle counting is a practical method to estimate battery age.

articleTitle: RTDS Dynamic Testing for Adaptive Defense Scheme on Several Subsystems in Java-Bali
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The increasing demand for operational services in power systems necessitates more sophisticated defense schemes to ensure system stability and prevent cascading failures or blackouts. Remedial Action Schemes (RAS) and Advanced Defense Schemes (ADS) have emerged as solutions to meet this requirement. In order to ensure the stability of the power system, it is essential to test the ADS before its implementation. Various testing methods are discussed, including simulation software testing, static open-loop testing, and dynamic testing using realtime simulators such as Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS). In the context of dynamic testing of ADS in Indonesia, a notable issue arises, the financial requirements associated with testing ADS developments using the RTDS create difficulties in terms of accessibility and utilization, limiting dynamic testing of ADS. The implementation of ADS by PLN units solely based on software simulation results that have not undergone RTDS dynamic testing poses significant risks. This can lead to potential failures or inadequate performance in critical situations. PLN Pusertif, as a Testing and Certification Institution within PLN Holding, plays a significant role in ensuring the quality of equipment used in the PLN power system and possesses an RTDS laboratory. This paper further explores the RTDS dynamic testing process conducted by PLN Pusertif for ADS, focusing on the case of PLN UIP2B Jamali and its implementation in multiple subsystems. The results of the dynamic testing demonstrate that the ADS design algorithms can effectively secure the power system from faults in each subsystem. This comprehensive testing approach plays a crucial role in the development and validation of the ADS, ensuring its functionality and reliability before its implementation in real power systems. The success of dynamic testing using the RTDS platform opens up opportunities for ADS development in other PLN Power System regions, reducing dependence on major manufacturers for conducting such tests.

articleTitle: Analysis of Forecast: Electricity Demand Energy of Sulawesi and Maluku 2060 Utilizing LEAP Application
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The Indonesian government by 2030 has placed a high priority on enhancing the quality and utilization of renewable energy to tackle energy and environmental challenges, aligning with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 9.4. To assess future trends in energy demand, consumption, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Indonesia from 2020 to 2060, various scenarios and sub-scenarios are analyzed. This study focuses on achieving NZE for consistency by 2060 through technology adoption and CO2 emission reductions, in line with the Paris Agreement’s objective of limiting global warming to 1.5°C and achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. The research emphasizes the significance of enhancing energy efficiency through demand-side management and energy-efficient technologies. These measures not only result in cost savings for households, businesses, industries, and the government but also contribute to carbon emission reductions. GHG emission projections utilize the Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) application. The Sulawesi region is expected to witness substantial growth in energy demand, particularly within the industrial sector. Key industries such as food and beverage production, tobacco, textiles and garments, leather and footwear, bamboo and rattan, paper, paper products, etc., are projected to experience significant increases in electricity demand. The growth rates for these sectors range from 5.09% to 37.1%, indicating a rising need for electricity to support various industrial processes. Notably, the total emissions in Sulawesi decreased impressively by 22.17% between 2021 and 2060. Similarly, the Maluku region demonstrates a promising trend of increasing electricity demand in the industrial sector, with an overall growth rate projected to be 5.93%. The food and beverage industry are expected to witness significant growth at a rate of 8.01%, while the textile and apparel sector and the pulp and paper sector are estimated to grow at rates of 9.02% and 9.22%, respectively. The total emissions in Maluku reduced significantly by 20.54%.

articleTitle: Influence of the Manufacture Process Parameters on the Dielectric Properties of a Composite Material for the Use in Dry Type Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Dry type transformers can be manufactured by means of vacuum cast coil technology (VCC) or filament winding process (FW). Coils fabricated by means of the filament winding technology, in which reinforcing mineral fiber filaments are impregnated with an organic resin, have a high mechanical robustness. Also, due to the fact of the high amount of reinforcing material, the coils can withstand higher mechanical stresses, having a minor amount of flammable material. In this contribution, the influence of different manufacturing process parameters on the dielectric behavior of a composite insulation material for dry-type transformers produced under the filament winding technology is investigated. The experimental results of measurements over the frequency f of the relative permittivity $\varepsilon_{r}$, the dissipation factor $\tan \delta$ and the electrical conductivity $\kappa$ of a composite insulation material, consisting of glass fiber filaments impregnated with epoxy resin, are presented. Six different production parameter variations were investigated. The measurements are performed in a frequency range between 10 Hz and 100 Hz considering the relevant operative values. Since the dielectric properties are strongly dependent on temperature, the measurements were performed at five different temperatures in a range between 50 °C and 120 °C. In general, the investigation shows an improvement in the dielectric parameters when the resin is vacuumed before the casting process. In that case, the dissipation factor $\tan \delta$ is reduced in around 20 % compared with the case in which the samples were manufactured without additional process. Also, the dependency on the temperature of the $\tan \delta$ is reduced. The application of vacuum during the curing process, as in the VCC technology, results contrarily in an impoverishment of the dielectric properties, leading to increasement of the dissipation factor near to the double of the base value and to high standard deviations on the measurements.

articleTitle: Estimation of Compression Dead-end Clamp Temperature to Identify Hot Spot of Transmission Power Line by Steady-State Heat Balance and Pitting Corrosion
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Corrosion on the compression dead-end clamp shoes, bolt, or nut can create a loose connection and leads to a hot spot. Due to the annealing effect, this hot spot will decrease the tensile strength of aluminum strand and steel core. For condition-based maintenance, the clamp and conductor temperature difference estimation identify a dead-end clamp hot spot. The difference is calculated by assuming the temperature is quadratic to the current. This assumption is inaccurate because of the balanced heat flow rule. This paper shows the implementation of a new equation to estimate clamp temperature by considering the ambient environment. The average estimation error of clamp temperature is 7.05% and conductor temperature is 4.32%. High estimation error can be caused by several unpredictable changing variables such as wind gusts and heat radiation of sun and clouds. Elevated temperature over a long period of operation time can be estimated by the pit corrosion growth. The corrosion rate increases further in the clamp high-temperature operation.

articleTitle: Simultaneously Optimization for Photovoltaic Battery and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The increase in electricity consumption is one of the phenomena that encourages an increase in the efficiency of electrical energy. Demand Response (DR) can be an option in managing the right demand side and providing meeting points for fluctuations in renewable energy generation. The DR program is oriented towards the consumer’s electricity consumption behavior related to electricity incentives. Planning for a Photovoltaic (PV) System is carried out to meet residential loads based on a peak clipping method approach during peak loads. There are 25 load-cutting scenarios that are simulated using HomerPro software to get the number of PV, battery and inverter. The result is a Levelized Cost Of Energy (LCOE) which can express the ratio of the cost of electricity generation to the electricity generated. The best LCOE value was found with a value of 0.286 USD/kWh at energy consumption of 409.58 kWh/day.

articleTitle: Optimization of Coal Fly Ash Filler Effect on Polymer Silicone Rubber Base Insulator Material on Dielectric Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: The addition of fly ash as a silicone rubber filler can increase the dielectric strength of the material, besides that the electrical test values are obtained from variations in the composition of the amount of fly ash in Room Temperature Vulcanization (RTV) silicone rubber. In this research, further studies were carried out to determine the optimization value of the composite characteristics of various variations in the composition of the amount of fly ash in RTV silicone rubber using the quadratic regression method and using RMSE to evaluate the level of accuracy of the model from the optimization results. This study carried out three types: breakdown voltage testing, volume resistivity testing, and surface resistivity to the amount of fly ash in RTV silicone rubber composite. After the test values were obtained using American Standard Testing and Materials (ASTM), composition optimization was continued using the quadratic regression method on the optimum composition of fly ash in RTV silicone rubber. The results obtained for the best composition of the three types of testing, the results of the breakdown voltage test obtained an optimum composition value of 50.88% with an RMSE value of 1.15 with an average percentage of 8.10%, then the volume resistivity test results obtained an optimum value composition of 29.90% with an RMSE value of 1.91 with an average percentage of 10.56%. The surface resistivity test results obtained an optimum composition value of 0.49% with an RMSE value of 12.86 with a percentage average of 6.52%.

articleTitle: An Approach for Planning Under Uncertainties for Indonesia’s Long-Term Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Indonesian government has stated its intention to achieve Net Zero Emission (NZE) by 2060. Yet there has been no official roadmap of energy transition issued by the government till today. This paper argues that scenario planning is needed to deal with uncertainties in distant futures. Those uncertainties are largely related to commercial maturity and costs of non-emitting technologies, as well as change of lifestyle in energy utilization. The paper argues that capacity expansion planning for the next 10 years is relatively visible, and the power projects can be made definitive. However, for longer terms, uncertainties will be very high. The paper also argues that making a roadmap with single pathway to distant future, complete with detail numbers and figures, would be not very useful. For this reason, this paper would argue that having scenario planning is more useful. It gives insights into some plausible trajectories for the longer term of energy transition when some ‘what-if circumstances prevail. Scenario planning is not intended to produce fixed and detail numbers and figures, instead it will provide insights into several plausible scenarios. The paper would show how scenario planning can be made for transition of Indonesia’s electricity sector toward low-carbon energy system.

articleTitle: Volt-Var Control for Utility-scale Solar PV Plants to Replace SVCs
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: One way to increase solar photovoltaic penetration in the grid is management of voltage fluctuations. This is because a photovoltaic plant cannot be interconnected to the grid if it causes voltage violations. Voltage violation is where voltage exceeds the acceptable range. Often, grid operators request photovoltaic plant owners to regulate voltage sufficiently with expensive and space-consuming static Var compensators. Unfortunately, this sometimes makes the project less feasible. This paper argues that there are better ways to regulate voltage. We ran a simulation with a 70 MWp photovoltaic plant as an addition to the grid. Without voltage regulation, voltage violations were found to be significant. This paper found that oversizing the inverter sufficiently would remove all voltage violations without deploying a static Var compensator. This is often a cheaper and space-saving solution for voltage management. This paper argues that economics and spatial efficiency of reactive power compensation devices is key to increasing photovoltaic penetration.
